reviews.title: Very nice Hotel, but not Kid friendly....
reviews.text: The bad: * Large packs of Super Karens and Kevins. Massive entitlement, they don't want to wait their turn...* Not really for kids. My kids are 9 to 11 years old, and the amount of dirty looks we received from Super Karens and Kevins, particularly when they were being kids playing in the pools, or lazy river was crazy. Karen and Kevin do not like any type of splashing near them. The Good:* Very clean room* Service by the cleaning lady was exceptional, she consistently checked in on us to see if we needed any water, ice, or towels.* Staff is quite friendly, and they have lots of patience. * The breakfast is very good. The steak dinner for the cost was meh...* It's quiet, compared to over hotels.

reviews.title: Outstanding Experience
reviews.text: We had an outstanding stay!The hotel is beautiful and the staff were so fantastic. Walked through many of the top resorts in Las Vegas during our stay and we were so glad that we chose the Four Seasons. While the other resorts were crowded, the Four Seasons was like an oasis of calm and tranquility.  A very special thank you to Assistant Guest Experience Manager Camille, who seemed to be everywhere for us when we needed any special assistance. I mentioned that I liked chocolate mousse and I was greeted with an amazing chocolate mousse cake on my birthday. The chocolate truffles, pistachio filled croissants, and welcome drinks were all amazing,some of best I have ever had, and unexpectedly easy to enjoy. There was virtually no wait for anything that we could ask for, despite the hotel serving so many professional basketball players  staying at the same time that we did. When we needed show and plane tickets printed unexpectedly, Camille and her staff took care of it. She was so incredibly kind, friendly and accommodating that we felt grateful to Camille and the rest of the amazing team there.  We have been fortunate to stay in some amazing resorts in our life, and this is truly one of the very best resorts in the world thanks to Camille and the rest of the amazing team there.

reviews.title: Great Stay at the Four Seasons Las Vegas
reviews.text: Enjoyed our experience from start to finish. The hotel is not in the heart of the strip and fit just what we wanted for a short weekend away in Las Vegas. If you are looking for a traditional casino experience, you can enjoy it by slipping into the connected Mandalay Bay and get back to the quiet of Four Seasons. Form our arrival, staff was warm and friendly. We checked in early and were offered a welcome beverage as well as a review of the amenities. A short walk from the lobby, through the shops/spa area are the elevators up to the guest rooms. The room we chose was spacious with a few cozy chairs and a small table to enjoy some room service. Room was clean,  well maintained with good lighting. The beds were extra comfortable as well. The bathroom offered a large tub but I did find the shower to be a bit tight. Enjoyed the Labor Day breakfast buffet ,which had a variety of yummy dishes to choose from. Everything we picked, was tasty. Overall from the room service, to breakfast and dinner I enjoyed the food during our stay. I’d recommend this hotel and definitely stay again!

reviews.title: Good Four Seasons without special features!
reviews.text: In itself a “normal” Four Seasons, similar to Chicago without much special features. The hotel is shared with Mandalay Bay. However, one does not come into contact with their gods. Room as usual clean and tidy. Great view from the room (for us as airplane fans) the runway from Harry Reid Intl. Valet reliable, friendly and fast. Price-wise very cheap. Probably due to the big competition within the city.

reviews.title: Great stay in Vegas!
reviews.text: I had a wonderful stay here this past weekend.  I booked through my travel advisor who had the Four Seasons amenities included in the booking.  The amenities included breakfast, a $100 credit, an upgrade at check in, etc.  I was able to check in early and was upgraded from my strip view room to a one bedroom suite overlooking the strip.  It was a beautiful room, comfortable bed, great bathrooms.  I loved my view overlooking the airport and the strip - it was perfect.  Service at the hotel was friendly and solicitous.  I spent two afternoons at the pool and service there was prompt.  Recommend the sin city burger for lunch.  I also had breakfast on the Press patio one morning and again the food was delicious and service great.  I was happy with the hotel's location - I loved how it's just a bit removed from the general hubbub of the strip but close enough to either do a good walk or easy cab/ uber.  I loved coming back both nights to what was definitely an oasis of tranquility after the busyness of the rest of the city.  I'd definitely return.

reviews.title: Love the Four Seasons
reviews.text: Love love, love the four seasons. The service is stellar. You cannot beat it. Loved Alicia at the front desk who gave us an opportunity to upgrade. We ended up with the nicest room and just decided to hang out all day and watch football because the room was so nice and comfortable. Room service was definitely yummy. The food was great. We had breakfast delivered the next morning. I wouldn’t change a thing about it. Luxury all the way, comfortable linen’s beautiful bedroom area we had the penthouse suite which just added extra extra ! Didn’t want to leave!! booked through American Express got the early check-in and late checkout plus credits!

reviews.title: Fantastic choice in Las Vegas - you'll love the Four Seasons!
reviews.text: Big thanks to Nicole Z and the entire staff at The Four Seasons in Las Vegas.  We have stayed at nearly all of the properties on the strip and hands down The Four Seasons is our new favorite. It feels entirely private, including a dedicated entrance (no walking a mile through a casino to get to your room), but should you want a Casino it's simply a stop on the elevator.  The rooms are elegant and perfectly appointed, incredibly clean and everything is simply first class. Our room has a fantastic strip view. We also enjoyed the room service, the quality of the ingredients and preparation of the food was excellent. Finally, all of the staff we encountered were friendly, professional and accommodating.  Quite simply, it's an outstanding hotel in every respect. A+.

reviews.title: great hotell
reviews.text: We had an amazing stay at the Four Seasons in Las Vegas. The hotel is beautiful, the rooms are spotless and comfortable, and the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome. The atmosphere is calm and relaxing — a perfect retreat from the busy Strip. We truly enjoyed every moment and are already looking forward to coming back. Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Relaxing oasis
reviews.text: 3rd time here but 1st since recent renno...Absolutely perfect!Quiet! No need walk thru casino...Rooms updated and so clean...Staff very friendly..Pool so relaxing..Really nice vibe...Pool lunch yummy...Fast check in...Easy to get to tram at Mandalay...Easy to go to Mandalay restaurants...And can go Mandalay pool - huge wave pool/beach etc....Highly recommend Four Seasons!

reviews.title: Best of both worlds
reviews.text: Hubby suggested a Vegas vacation, but I wanted to relax. We chose Four Seasons because it is a non-smoking property without a casino; however, you can access the Mandalay Bay casino if you want to gamble. One great thing about the property is that we could access Mandalay Bay's lazy river and wave pool, which was very crowded, and then return to our more upscale, relaxing pool for the rest of the day. Also, it is worth noting that at Mandalay Bay and other less expensive hotels, you have to pay for a lounge chair with an umbrella by the pool. At Four Seasons, it's included. So, if you think you're getting a better deal elsewhere, you might not be, as other places nickel and dime you to death for everything instead of treating you like a valued guest.We also loved the hotel's bed and pillows. They are the most comfortable of anywhere we have stayed. Also, all the staff were genuinely friendly.

reviews.title: Another Extraordinary Experience
reviews.text: We had a remarkable experience during our stay. The facilities are impeccably clean, of the highest quality, and the views are breathtaking. However, it is the exceptional staff that truly distinguishes this hotel. I would like to extend my gratitude to the following individuals:Camille Bagnol arranged an extraordinary Las Vegas-themed amenity for my birthday, which served as a delightful surprise for my mother, whom I see only once a year. I have included photographs of the room arrangement with this review.Thomas LaCentra regularly checked on us and provided two delightful amenities. He oversees an exemplary Room Service Department.Peter Kamau facilitated our access to a cabana, ensuring that we enjoyed a wonderful experience by the pool.Jarrod Ray contributed significantly to our enjoyable time at the pool on each day of our visit.Nicole Zvek personally introduced herself during our check-out and guaranteed that I had a pleasant departure experience.Zlata and Snjezana were outstanding poolside servers, ensuring that we had excellent experiences throughout our stay.Doug Ward was responsible for managing all of our dining and activity reservations, and he exhibited great attention to detail in addressing special requests.

reviews.title: Unfortunately the Four Seasons didn't fulfil our expectations
reviews.text: This trip was a one off for us and as a special treat we thought we'd stay at one of the premium hotels in Las Vegas. Obviously the cost was significant as expected and we were very much looking forward to our stay.Prior to our visit we were asked 3 times what time we'd be arriving. Once via the website reservation preferences and then twice via e-mails from the front of house team. Not a big deal, but was a little surprising.On arrival we were greeted by a member of the reception team who offered us a welcome drink of water in what I can only describe as a small cardboard milk type of container, no glass. This was surprising as very much lesser hotels we've stayed at offer a glass of juice or sparkling wine on arrival. We asked the lady about the breakfast hours and arrangements. She didn't seem to know the hours or the offering, but "thought" a buffet may be available at the weekend and table service the rest of the time. Again, very surprising as surely it would be a standard requirement for the reception team to know this? Once checked in a (hefty) pre hold was taken on our credit card and she asked if we required help with our cases. When we said no, the lady walked us to the corridor and vaguely  pointed in the direction of the elevators.On booking I had requested a room in a specific area which had been granted, so that was a positive. The room itself was very nice, the bed and bedding was lovely. The air conditioning was good, but relatively noisy compared to some. Also every time the guests in the next door room flushed their toilet or emptied their sink, there was a loud gurgling noise from our bathroom sink. A number of TV channels were not available for some reason. This seemed to be a signal fault, but we didn't report it as we weren't going to spend much time watching TV. Housekeeping was very good and the evening turn down service where the ice bucket was replenished was also very good. However on our last day the housekeeping team tried to access our room in the morning and seemed unaware that we were actually checking out that day. Probably not their fault, but down to communication from the reception team.The breakfast service was good and the pool service excellent. Generally the staff were very nice and friendly. However, one morning when I asked at reception about booking a taxi the lady said it was nothing to do with them and to speak to concierge, which I did, to be told to just wait outside and a taxi would hopefully be along soon! I decided to use an Uber from there on. Overall I would say that we were a little disappointed with our stay for the price paid and the standard of hotel. I would respectfully suggest that the front of house staff probably would benefit from additional training as first impressions count, especially at a hotel of this quality and status.

reviews.title: Pretty Typical Four Seasons
reviews.text: Excellent service . Clean well appointed room. All staff very accommodating. Willow at room service made an effort to communicate when it was super late. Kudos to her for doing her job very well. Wish the Amex benefits were better as they usually are in other Four Seasons we have stayed at. Like the vibe and the secret door to the Mandalay Casino. A good option on the strip for those of us who want to experience Vegas on our own terms. Spa very good.

reviews.title: The best of the best!
reviews.text: This is by far our favorite hotel in Vegas! We have been coming to the area for 30 years, and the service and rooms are better than any other hotel hands down. We have stayed here multiple times in the past year and already have more stays booked! The staff is wonderful, and the rooms are beautiful. The bedding is fantastic and we rested great. Thank you to Nicole for always helping us with our reservations, Camille for checking on us, and Moses for the warm welcome and helpfulness. The staff is fantastic, and we look forward to being here soon for our next visit.

reviews.title: It’s in the details
reviews.text: It’s in the details. Four Seasons Las Vegas did not disappoint from pre check in to check out.Prior to checking in, I was specific in my request for a room near the elevators and it was granted at check in. I even asked if they could do a little something for my daughter’s softball tournament (which was why we were in Vegas). They wrote a card wishing her luck with a display of chocolates, popcorn and root beer in the room. Super thoughtful! The room was overall spotless, but there were a few crumbs on the carpet and the shower door had a large gap (where water would leak to the outside of the bathroom floor). I think housekeeping was aware because they provided extra towels to soak up the water. I was grateful because I didn’t have to ask. The food at Press and Bourbon was on point! Delicious food with great service. Could not ask for anything more. The valet was always busy to the point they forgot to help with who was checking in (incl us with our luggage).On the day of check out and after doing so, our daughter’s team won their softball tournament and she was covered in dirt. We had an extra hour before heading to the airport and the front desk said we could return to use the showers in the spa to get her cleaned up. Now, that’s service! All in all, we had a great stay with a few issues but nothing to take a star away. This gem of a hotel is wonderful for people who value the details and want to stay on the strip, but don’t want to deal with the crowds and smoke of Vegas.

reviews.title: As always a classy and quiet hotel with all the Vargas excitement immediately available
reviews.text: This is my fifth visit to the Four Seasons Las Vegas, and I always find myself returning. The rooms are spacious and the beds are incredibly comfortable. The bathrooms come with both a shower and a bathtub, which is a nice touch. I was lucky enough to get a pool view, just as I requested. What I appreciate most about this hotel is that it doesn’t have a casino, which creates a peaceful and sophisticated atmosphere. However, if you're in the mood for some action, it's easy to step through a door and access Mandalay Bay (and the tram).The pool area is another highlight. It's beautiful, not overcrowded, and the staff is always attentive, ensuring you're well taken care of. Plus, you're granted full access to all of Mandalay Bay’s pools. This hotel strikes the perfect balance between a serene and luxurious experience, while still offering all the excitement of Las Vegas, depending on your "mood of the day."

reviews.title: An Anniversary Trip and First Time in Las Vegas for the books!
reviews.text: This review is the subjective opinion of an individual traveller and not of Tripadvisor LLC nor of its partners. Tripadvisor performs checks on reviews as part of our industry-leading trust & safety standards. Read our transparency report to learn more.

reviews.title: Two Seasons at best.
reviews.text: We have been lucky enough to stay in many Four Seasons properties around the world over the years.  They are expensive however they have generally been beautiful locations providing exceptional service and small gestures of attentiveness which made the investment feel like it was more than worth it. Unfortunately, that formula isn’t present in Las Vegas.There are, of course, some positives.  First, the rooms are well equipped, comfortable and spotlessly clean.  Second, we had great service from the member of the team who helped us up to our room with our bags and spent time showing us our room, giving us some ideas of where to visit and getting us some extra water. Housekeeping staff and our waiter at breakfast were also friendly and helpful.The property itself is a disappointment.  The location at the end of the strip is pretty bad with awful views and a fairly grim walk if you want to go and see the more lively parts of the strip.  The concept is also flawed as the hotel is located on a few floors of the huge Mandalay Bay resort.  When you sit outside in the small external area around the pool, you are surrounded by Mandalay Bay buildings and branding. At best, staying here feels like you are staying at what could be described as the executive floors of the Mandalay Bay.Front of house is awful and two areas really disappointed - reception and the team that greet you for breakfast.  The reception team lack warmth and are clearly understaffed.  Whilst we didn’t have to wait long to check in, the experience was perfunctory at best.  Checking out was horrible. We were leaving around 0800 and had allowed time as we had a tight schedule.  There was only one lady on reception and she was dealing with a problem for a customer.  After waiting quite a while, I asked her politely if she could call someone else.  I should not have had to ask, there was little apology and I felt like I was just an annoying piece of administration.  She did call and eventually another man arrived.  I explained we were now in a rush and his response was just to ask me how long I had waited and say he would mention my feedback to a manager.  When he had logged in, there was then a problem with our bill because our breakfast that morning hadn’t been listed which was odd given we had room service that morning and had ordered it the night before to facilitate a quick departure.  In the end, he gave me a credit on my bill which I didn’t want and didn’t ask for, making me feel like he was doing me a favour when in fact all I wanted was to pay what I owed and not wait any longer.The reason we had breakfast in our room the second morning is the restaurant breakfast experience is also poor mainly due to the team who greet you on arrival. There is no welcome at the desk, they print tickets with your name and stick them to a rather worn area of the counter where you then wait until someone comes to take you to the table.  The young lady who eventually took us lacked any warmth and didn’t seem interested in answering questions about the buffet.  We felt dumped at our seats and we have had certainly had better welcomes in budget cafes. There are two areas to eat, one very noisy and messy and one slightly better but a long way from the buffet.  Our waiter was very helpful when we finally sat down but again this was not a Four Seasons experience.Concierge did help us before we arrived with a restaurant booking and they were very helpful.  Oddly though, the concierge seems to be closed in the evening, even on a Saturday night when you might often want help.  This just feels like a cost cutting exercise which isn’t consistent with expectations of the Four Seasons brand.Finally there are none of the small gestures that you get at other Four Seasons properties.  No bedtime chocolates or other small amenities that we have always received before although there were two small cakes on arrival.  They aren’t needed but you do kind of expect them with the Four Seasons brand.  There were other small problems like a very squeaky door to our bathroom and an already used and opened carton of water next to our bed when we checked in.Finally, it all just felt totally impersonal.  We have been loyal to the Four Seasons brand for decades and there was no recognition of that loyalty.Sadly we will not return and this has also made us question whether our loyalty is now misplaced.

reviews.title: Mostly an exceptional experience, as usual
reviews.text: I stay at this hotel primarily because it is smoke and vape  free, including all of the common areas, and they enforce the policy. They do have one designated smoking place that is rather ill conceived as it sits under a ceiling so the area smells like an ashtray and one must walk by it on the way to the gym. Hopefully they will reconsider.But, the hotel is a super stay, exactly what one would expect from a FS.On this latest trip I want to highlight the pool staff ( so welcoming and helpful) as well as f and b poolside. I ordered a tuna roll and it was spectacular, the fish was cold and fresh, and it was served with plenty of wasabi, ginger and soy sauce- an exceptional snack, reasonably priced- Kudos to the chef and his/her team 🙏🏼I do wish all hotels, including this one, that have adopted the “ resort fee” practice - in this case $55 per day- would be transparent about it and just increase the room rate so that guests can make an informed decision. Yes, I get dynamic pricing and psychology but  the way it is done now is rather deceptive and IMHO the FS is better than that.Did not take away from another great stay but just be mindful.

reviews.title: Not perfect but we were happy to stay here
reviews.text: I do love four seasons as our stays there across the country have been pretty consistent. We were happy to stay here after a long trip visiting national parks with some rustic lodging. I love that this hotel is off the strip and much quieter, and you’re not walking through smoky, crowded casinos to get to your room. And the service here is quite good. That being said, we were completely disappointed in the breakfast buffet. It’s exorbitantly priced, and although the selections are quite varied, most of the food was cold to lukewarm. Management made it right, but I expected better for a four seasons.

reviews.title: Quiet, luxurious hotel on the quieter end of the Strip, Las Vegas
reviews.text: The Four Seasons occupies floors 35-39 of the Mandalay Bay hotel. There is a separate entrance and a dedicated reception and lobby, with a separate gym, spa, and some shops. Otherwise the hotel will direct you to the Mandalay Bay for restaurant recommendations. Pros: - service was excellent and felt personal. - rooms spacious and very clean. - coffee machine with pods in the rooms, a water station on every floor. - nice amenities in the room (products from Nature Bisse). - hotel is on quieter end and not crowded. Cons:- located very south of the Strip so it is a far distance to the centre of the Strip. There is however a monorail service connecting Mandalay Bay to New York, New York which helps save time. - not much happening at this end of the Strip, and the closest hotels to the Four Seasons (Mandalay Bay, Luxor, and Excalibur) aren’t great. All in all, very much enjoyed our stay!

reviews.title: Nice hotel but average service
reviews.text: The Four Seasons Hotel Las Vegas offers a luxurious experience with spacious and comfortable rooms that ensure a restful stay. The staff is friendly and attentive, consistently providing excellent service. However, dining experiences at the hotel’s restaurants were disappointing. At Bourbon Steak Las Vegas, we waited 30 minutes for a server to take our order and another 30 minutes to pay. Similarly, at Veranda, the ordering process felt superficial, and mistakes occurred on two separate days. While the hotel excels in accommodations and hospitality, improvements in restaurant service are necessary to match its high standards. It seems that the Four Seasons Hotels are only expensive and the services are like regular hotels.

reviews.title: Nickel & Diming Galore......
reviews.text: I've been to the Four Seasons Las Vegas at least 4 or 5 times over the last few years.Was at the hotel over Thanksgiving weekend and that will certainly be the last time.Booked through AMEX FHR as I always do.Found out upon checking in that the hotel provides $75 per couple toward breakfast, which is only a Continental Breakfast.   They are very up-front about that as it is printed on the AMEX FHR Welcome Letter.    (Obviously they know that it insufficient for a full breakfast entitlement because if you book the Breakfast Package directly through the Four Seasons Website, they offer $90.)    That's shady!Continental Breakfast is juice, pastry and coffee or tea.  As someone who has booked hotels though AMEX FHR for over 9 years this is the first time I've had a hotel tell me, "we're only obligated to offer you Continental Breakfast."Furthermore, a Manager, justified this nonsense by telling me we offer you the 4pm checkout and $125 spa credit.  Um, that perk is automatic from AMEX FHR, NOT the so-called generosity of the hotel.  So nice try on that excuse.Finally, this one I knew before booking but its still nickel and diming at its core.The hotel charges a $55 resort fee, even in the Winter.   The so-called resort fee is for use of the hotel pools, lazy river, phone calls, etc.   Considering that 99% of the world has a cell phone and PLUS its November and the pools are CLOSED! No one is swimming/tanning;  its outrageous and offensive to charge for something that isn't available.While the hotel is within their right to charge whatever fees they like, I am within my right to patronize a different hotel that doesn't feel the need to fleece their guests.ZERO chance I'd return.

reviews.title: Incredible Class, Among the Best Hotel Experiences in My Life
reviews.text: The staff at this hotel was incredible.  I have never been treated with such class and professionalism over many decades.   Every single team member should be proud of their efforts and obviously the training is incredible.This hotel is an oasis within Vegas.  I have stayed at Vdara for many years, as it is one of the few hotels not attached to a casino.  The same is true of Four Seasons, but it is much more sequestered, but in a brilliantly clever way.Near the elevators to the rooms, there is a door that leads you into Mandalay Bay.  But before you go through that door, you feel as if you are in a private, rarified space.  You would barely know you are in Vegas, in terms of the quiet and serenity.The turndown and housekeeping service was beyond incredible.  I made sure to leave around $4-5 bucks each morning and evening for housekeeping as a means of requesting a little extra attention, but whether or not that was a factor, the service was incredible.  They organized my items and put ties on my charging cords during turndown.  The room was recleaned and restocked.I had a rather embarrassing incident my last morning where I thought my iPad had been stolen while I was in the bathroom.  Foolishly, I had failed to check the coffee area where I had in fact left it.  Before this was discovered, I alerted staff to a potential theft.  In a discrete but very conscientous way, they swung into motion including looking at footage.  Upon finding it at the coffee stand, the most obvious statement in the world would have been "you left it at the coffee stand."  However, all they did was very discretely hand me the iPad and indicate they had found it at the coffee stand.  In short, every effort was made to avoid having me feel blamed for what was in fact a silly thing on my  behalf that riled everyone up.What strikes me also is that the staff was not exuberantly friendly in some kind of flamboyant manner.  Folks were very friendly, but in an entirely classy and even understated manner.  I can scarcely imagine the training that went into all of this, but it paid off.I really enjoyed the mellow lobby were you could sit and have coffee in the morning or a drink at night.  They also had fire pits going by the pool.What's important to note is that, as far as I can tell, the Four Seasons is part of the Mandalay Bay and is on the upper rooms.  I was given a room on the very top floor.  When they say "strip view," they mean in.  This property is at the very beginning of the strip, so I had a panoramic view of the entire strip.  The floor to ceiling windows made this even more mesmerizing.I have no idea how these rooms compare to those at Mandalay Bay, but my room was large and very well-proportioned.  There was a shower and bathtub, and certainly touches like a bathrobe.In any event, the elevator blasts through the lower floors and there you are on floors 35 and up.The Four Seasons has a dedicated swimming pool, although guests can also use the Mandalay Bay pool.  This helps with the feeling of a private oasis.  In candor, the pool is not large -- it's pretty basic.  I imagine the privacy would still come in handy.  Due to the coolness of the weather, I did not swim.I have never stayed at a Four Seasons, so I don't know how it compares.  However, the aesthetic of this property is not gaudy -- it's classy.  The staff is the core of the experience.  They believe strongly in their mission and nothing reasonable is spared in terms of making their guests feel pampered.This is easily in the top two experiences I have ever had at a hotel.  It's also worth considering that with the large Vegas properties -- even the classier ones -- there appear to be significant inconsistencies in service.  Which isn't surprising given the overall economy and the challenges of a huge property.This is a smaller oasis with serenity, tremendous quiet, and class in all respects.I am truly grateful for this stay and how I was treated.

reviews.title: Hate Vegas, LOVE this Four Seasons!
reviews.text: Love this Four Seasons! The service is perfection and it's the only hotel we stay at in Las Vegas. We stay a couple times a year and it's always a pleasant experience. This past trip last month I need a little something special and Kalmeeta Solanky in the spa went above and beyond to make sure I was taken care of. Thank you FSV! See again soon

reviews.title: Perfect rooms and top notch staff!
reviews.text: We have been coming to Vegas for 30 years, and this hotel is our new favorite. We have stayed multiple times this year and will be here several times in 2025. The service, accommodations, and 100% nonsmoking atmosphere makes the entire stay outstanding. Nicole, the director of rooms, has been so helpful for arranging our stays and helping with our room selection so it is perfect. The front desk team, housekeepers, and staff outside assisting with vehicles are also fantastic. Everyone is very friendly and helpful. We look forward to coming back soon and staying with you again - thank you!

reviews.title: Will Stay Again
reviews.text: Great hotel at one end of the strip.  I love how people talk about there's no casino - which is true - but there's literally a "trap door" to get into the Mandalay Bay casino.  So, you get the best of both worlds at FS.  You will be met by multiple people every time you arrive, return or depart.   The rooms are quite large and recently re-done.  The lobby and bar area are nice, smaller and quiet compare to what you find in LV.  Weekend brunch is the legendary version this hotel brand has offered since the 1990's.  We will definitely stay again.  Easy check in and check out - similar to another hotel within a hotel along the strip.  Buyer beware:  The Spa Bar is no longer walk-in and traffic along the strip is at an all-time insane high.

reviews.title: Great stay at a wonderful hotel
reviews.text: Hotel was fantastic. From housekeeping to concierge, everything was top notch. Made my stay very enjoyable. Conference area was great and food was fantastic. The main thing that made my stay more enjoyable was the attentiveness of the staff. Always nice to be greeted by a room attendant or maintenance staff.

reviews.title: Wonderful service and great room.
reviews.text: We had a wonderful stay at the Four Seasons Las Vegas.  The room was big and very comfortable with a great view.  Bathroom with the shower and bath tub met our expectations for a Four Seasons resort.  The location worked out perfectly as our main event was the Chiefs/Raiders game at Allegiant Stadium.  Loved the oasis this hotel provided for us with the pool, lobby bar and Veranda restaurant.  All the staff we encountered were very nice and helpful from check-in to check-out.  In particular Lauren in the Veranda restaurant.  We had lunch there multiple times and she always remembered us and gave us wonderful service.

reviews.title: Disappointing Experience at Four Seasons Las Vegas
reviews.text: I stayed at the Four Seasons Las Vegas for one night, expecting the high level of service that the brand is known for. Unfortunately, my experience fell far short of that standard.Upon checking into my room, I noticed a brown stain on my bed, so I called down to request fresh sheets. No one ever came to replace them, but I did receive a polite apology email through my Expedia profile. While the apology was appreciated, I would have preferred if someone had actually come and addressed the issue.Room service that evening was also disappointing. I ordered a burger and asked specifically for extra condiments, but none arrived. After waiting for 15 minutes, ketchup was finally brought up—by then, my food was cold and unenjoyable. I also ordered the seasonal cheesecake, which I was told would be mango-flavored, but I received a plain cheesecake with a side of blackberries instead.Overall, the experience felt more like a budget hotel than a luxury stay. Given the many other options in Las Vegas for the same price, I wouldn’t recommend this particular Four Seasons. It just didn’t live up to the brand’s reputation.

reviews.title: Sanctity in the heart of it all
reviews.text: This hotel is in the Mandalay Bay. It's nice to have a seaprate entrance and elevator. It has a more mellow vibe. It allowsa you to have all the fun and excitement of Vegas, but then slip away to someplace peaceful to regain your energy.Very elegant and nice people and service. A quiet pool, too!

reviews.title: Continues to Be a Stellar Hotel in Vegas
reviews.text: We go to Vegas a lot, and love staying at the myriad of wonderful hotels there.  But this is in the top 3.Service is the best, bar none.  It’s wonderful to always see not 1, but at least 2 or more at the concierge desk and check-in.  Terrific.  Ditto for the fact you do not need to walk through a casino to get to check-in or the elevators.  Valet service is wonderful and prompt.So many Vegas hotels are so large and impersonal.  This one is on the top 5 floors of Mandalay Bay, and a world apart.  It’s quiet, beautifully decorated, and intimate.It’s also close to the Allegiant Stadium, another beauty, if you’re going to a big concert or game there.  There’s a walkway that leads from Manadalay to the stadium, making it easy to access (but a good walk so wear comfortable shoes).We were there several years ago when the rooms were more dated.  They’ve since done a great reno on the rooms, with a cool contemporary look.  They’re spacious, and have great views due to the oversized windows and fact they’re 35+ stories up.Bathroom however still looks dated (vanity).  Water pressure and showerhead are awesome.  Toilet room was frustrating as there’s a heavy door to access, and it doesn’t stay open—had to put  the garbage can to prop it open. Frustrating.Also wish they could find a great replacement from the former Charlie Palmer Steakhouse.  But there are a lot of options in Mandalay Bay, and easy to access—the “C” button in the elevator takes you to the casino floor there.

reviews.title: Young Woman Business Trip
reviews.text: From check-in to check-out, I was heard and seen. I felt safe and cared for. The team at the four seasons did not skip a beat and made sure to take into consideration I was a young woman travelling alone for business. Would stay again and again!!

reviews.title: Best place to return to in Las Vegas.
reviews.text: The best team in Las Vegas.  Friendly, professional and efficient.  The food is excellent with a lot of options.  Great scene in the evening and a power breakfast for sure.  The rooms are completely quiet, clean, modern and the most comfortable bed ever.

reviews.title: Absolutely best stay in Vegas
reviews.text: We have stayed here several times over the last 23 years, and it keeps getting better. Having found many experiences lacking after Covid, this is especially lovely to find a place exceeding expectations. Ever single person we interacted with starting with the reservation agent I spoke with to the last bell person that put us in a taxi to the airport was exceedingly pleasant and helpful. Absolutely the best place to stay in Vegas:Room is large, we had a  beautiful view of strip, room was quiet, tons of amenities like multiple plugs, white noise machine, speaker to play music. Slippers,  robes, child friendly amenities. Ask for fridge for your own usage, we are not a fan of mini bar fridge.Rollaway bed was comfortable, book in advance.Plenty of water and water bottle refill station near elevator, so logical to have and so helpful Pool:: exceptional service , from setting up towels,  umbrellas, floats to take to Mandalay Bay, water pitchers, quiet,  easy access to lazy river and wave pool. I don't think I can emphasize enough how great the service is by the pool.  There's even sunscreen available. I will never stay anywhere else in Vegas solely based on the pool service. Veranda: brunch best ever, plan around it, really! breakfast, lunch (by the pool), supper amazing. At some point a fancy restaurant will open here but the Veranda kitchen puts out first rate food. Don't be disuaded by lack of a name. Great wine list.Bell/transportation staff helpfulEvening bar service, underrated yet so good.Welcoming to kids and celebrating our anniversary, so kind.Beautiful spaWe rented a  car at Mandalay bay Avis (costco) to go to grand canyon, highly recommend. Here you have the best of both worlds, quiet refuge in the Vegas strip yet access to all the things you came to Vegas for.

reviews.title: Exceptional Service
reviews.text: The night we checked in Kamala was staying at the hotel too. In front of the hotel there were a whole bunch of SUVs. When we entered there was a swarm of secret service, police with ARs, and dogs. That said they were friendly toward us.I felt the service was exceptional. When we called and needed something they responded immediately. I would say in light of all the places that I I have stayed this was probably the best service that we got. This is trip in Vegas was probably the best trip my wife and I had, and we have traveled a bit.Also the concierge was very helpful. There is no casino in the hotel, however if you choose floor “C” you go into the casino in Mandalay Bay. At the time there was a big emergency medicine doctor convention there.I did feel that the breakfast there was kind of pricy. For a simple breakfast I felt it’s more than I wanted to spend. Other than the first morning we went to buffets at other hotels for breakfast.I would highly recommend this hotel. We also had a beautiful room.

reviews.title: Fighting Moths
reviews.text: There were moths in my room every day. The hotel staff was very friendly and tried to suggest a fix, but the only option was to cover my vents. With it being over 100º every day during my stay, I had to decide between not dealing with the moths and staying cool and comfortable. I decided to keep them uncovered to keep my room cool.

reviews.title: the best of the best
reviews.text: This was our second time with Four Seasons as I am now addicted! From the concierge app service to the luxury of the brand there simply is no other Hotel that compares. Classy always clean and prompt KIND service always. The location is perfect and upon returning you feel like you are in your own special Vegas Oasis. Best Hotel Ever and the only way to go.

reviews.title: This hotel is a do NOT miss!
reviews.text: I am the pickiest hotel guest imaginable. This hotel stay was perfect. It was spotless. The service was a 10. The food was delicious. I can’t say one negative thing. If you are bringing kiddos to Vegas this spot is perfect. I can’t wait to come back!

reviews.title: Great hotel.
reviews.text: Amazing experience. Professional service, luxury rooms and facilities in a very welcoming and safe environment.

reviews.title: Calm Oasis in Vegas
reviews.text: I can’t fault this hotel. It is a calm oasis within vegas. The staff can’t do enough, rooms are beautiful and a lovely relaxing pool. You benefit from access to Mandalay Bay if you wish to use their pools (we only popped across once). Room service was great and highly recommend.

reviews.title: 10 out of 10
reviews.text: My wife and I LOVED this property! Few shout outs- Esther at the front desk was so delightful and made us feel so welcomed and right at home. We also had such a wonderful conversation and experience with Leakhena at breakfast! What a lovely dining experience and great recommendation on the Steak and Eggs! By far the best we’ve had! Kudos to all the staff front and back of house at Veranda! The food was superb. You all went out of your way to make my wife’s birthday extra special.This is the only place we will ever stay in Las Vegas. The pool is wonderful as well. The service was excellent and we enjoyed the scenery/privacy and the escape from all the hustle and bustle at Mandalay. 10 out of 10 team! We are so grateful for you!

reviews.title: Great hotel
reviews.text: Fantastic hotel. Staff more than willing to help out, lovely rooms and amenities. Turn down service left cakes which was a really nice touch. Good proximity to the rest of the strip via a shuttle train to the Mandalay bay. Overall really recommend.

reviews.title: Serene paradise
reviews.text: Lovely hotel next to the Mandalay Bay with its own private entrance. We chose this establishment because it is a non smoking hotel and not a crowded casino.The service is what you would expect from a Four Seasons establishment, very stellar and the work staff caters to your every need.The lobby is beautiful with gorgeous flower displays and marble floors.Even though it was quite hot  (105°) I did visit the pool one morning to relax, and the young lady working the towels set me up with nice lounge, chairs and ice water in a pitcher with a glass. The pool is small and very private with mini lounge, chairs and areas to sit with umbrellas intermittently, a little snack such as a frozen pineapple, lollipop, strawberry smoothie and chocolate covered blueberries were served to me as I relaxed. such a nice touch.The room is very comfortable with a very large bathroom marble floors, muted colors in taupe and light brown made for a very serene sleeping experience. We had a wonderful view of the strip, which was very nice at night with the neon lights brightly shining , and and the Sphere in the distance changing colors.This hotel is a quiet paradise away from the madness of the casinos and the Las Vegas strip. Our go to in Las Vegas!

reviews.title: Excellent Las Vegas Hotel
reviews.text: Excellent Hotel. Nicely Separated from heavy casino traffic, pool near Veranda Restaurant quiet, private, protected from direct sun, small but important plus for lounging poolside in hot summer hours. Hotel not overwhelmed by, but connect to casino via access through private floor entrance to Mandalay Bay. Rooms well designed, service top notch. Restaurants great quality. Is it expensive? Yes, but it’s a great choice for the discriminating, high-dollar traveler who sees gambling as simply one of many curiosities for coming to or driving through Las Vegas.

reviews.title: As you would expect...
reviews.text: Wonderful time in the heart of Las Vegas. Nice to have a hotel without a casino where you can escape. Its private and personal, but by walking down one hallway, you can connect to several other casino hotels. Impeccable service and great food.

reviews.title: Excellent Stay
reviews.text: Beautiful Room, Fantastic ServiceAny special request: just let the know and they will resolve any request.

reviews.title: Magical stay with family
reviews.text: Extraordinary staff, serene room, and the most relaxing pool in Vegas. Perfect hotel for a family with young children.

reviews.title: First Class in Vegas
reviews.text: My family and I did a short trip to Vegas for a concert and were very pleased with the experience at the Four Seasons. We travel alot and from arrival to departure the service and overall experience was as expected from a Four Seasons. Our room was clean, well-executed and quiet.  We are not smokers nor gamblers so the lack of the "Vegas Experience" of smoke, noise and the crowds enhanced improved our trip.

reviews.title: A calm oasis...
reviews.text: What a delightful way to enjoy Las Vegas. The Four Seasons was the bit of calm I needed for retreat from the crowds and chaos. The staff was outstanding, the room was comfortable, calming, and well-appointed, and the pool was tranquil.

reviews.title: Won’t be staying here again
reviews.text: For what I paid for my stay, the room never got cold even at night, the internet in my room was intermittent and the cell phone coverage was terrible. The room was old and wasn’t cleaned well upon arriving.

reviews.title: It’s all changed for the worst.
reviews.text: Well here goes, I waited until I returned home to do this review. We've been longtime FSH clients, been to numerous FS over a span of ten years or so, always faithful to the brand. Living in Las Vegas, we'd spend every other weekend throughout the year at this location for the luxury, fabulous food and service. Well those days are apparently over, after eight nights in a studio suite (booked on points, couldn't cancel) at this location, we won't be returning. First off, since they've gotten into the mattress selling biz, they've downgraded their mattresses to make a profit. Their 'plush top' was like sleeping on concrete. I had to jimmyrig it with Euro pillows, it still was hard as a rock. The rooms are no longer luxurious, they are cold with a touch of communist grey. The food is fine, but you pay top dollar for just fine. We spent the majority of time at the pool, but it's changed in just a year as well. Seems they are really going for the whole DEl thing, hard.They give off a vibe that's uninviting towards to vacationers, more geared towards the DEI/ESG worker bees. And we refuse to partake in their 'wokeness' with their teeny tiny cartons of water. The cans sucked, the the cartons of water are just as awful. Figi anyone? We'd been planning on a vacation to the FS Maui or Lanai, but nope, can't imagine after what we've just experienced. Goodbye Four Seasons, it was nice knowing you.

reviews.title: An oasis for adults on the strip
reviews.text: Stayed for two nights at the end of July. The Rooms were updated, large, and very clean. Staff were exceptionally friendly, from the front desk to the shops, spa, and pool. We enjoyed returning to our room to find nice little touches from the cleaning crew. The exercise room is well equipped and probably the nicest hotel gym I’ve ever been inside. Also, I was very grateful to receive a lower rate on my room at checkin, having noticed that rates were nearly half of what i had paid when booking the reservation six weeks prior.It was nice to have access to the Mandalay Bay pools, but they were overcrowded to the point that it was uncomfortable - The lazy river wasn’t even moving, it was so full of people!  So it was very nice to come back to the quiet and relaxing four seasons pool. If you do wander to the Mandalay Bay pools, we were told that the four seasons has floats for the lazy river for guests to borrow so you can avoid spending $35/float. The only low point we experienced was that the umbrellas at the pool were lowered in the middle of the afternoon due to occasional wind. My Irish friend could not handle the sun, so we weren’t able to spend as much time at the pool as we had wanted or planned. I understand the circumstances but surely there are umbrellas out there that can better handle wind, and a 5-star hotel in Vegas can offer pool-side shade to their guests in middle of summer.Overall, i would definitely return. It’s a great escape from the chaos that is the Vegas strip, an adult oasis in the desert.

reviews.title: Will return
reviews.text: Room was excellent. Peaceful hotel.  Staff were all helpful and friendly especially Carlos in the spa. We ate twice at Veranda restaurant with excellent service and food. I thought it was good for what we got and will definitely return.  It’s close to the airport so Kevin is not a big expense. There is a McDonald’s across the street so if you want reasonably price coffee, you can cross the street and avoid the charge in the lobby, which was not cheap. But all in all we loved it.

reviews.title: A restful retreat
reviews.text: This is the place to fully relax and leave the details to others. Every request filled, every need met.

reviews.title: Nice stay away from gambling but not too far away
reviews.text: This hotel was nice, it was off the strip and didn’t have a casino. Nice for a getaway. The walk to the Mandalay Bay wasn’t terribly far and there’s a secret door which leads you right to an escalator and then from there you’re basically in the lobby. it was very clean. The spa was decent although I wasn’t sure what other amenities they had available in the spa. Breakfast at the local restaurant there was really good food and top-notch service. They really want the extra mile with their service all around. Will revisit.

reviews.title: First Rate Check-in Experience
reviews.text: I wanted to especially give kudos to Julia P. who was so cheerful and friendly as she checked us in. She acknowledge that we were Four Seasons Residence Club owners at a different resort, and offered to upgrade our room.  The complimentary bottled water she provided were definitely appreciated given the 100+ outside temperatures at the time.  Other staff we encountered at the Four Seasons were also very friendly.

reviews.title: Amazing service and luxurious comfort
reviews.text: Where to begin? You know you are in a special place when after year after year for more than 10 years I see the same faces. It says a lot about the hotel that the staff choose to stay. The pool attendants, Andres and Jarrod are always there ready to greet me with a friendly smile when I arrive. They ensure the water is cold and plentiful. The staff that attends to our hunger and thirst are always amazing: a special shout out to Djanna, Noah, Salde and Slata who work tirelessly. May at breakfast at Verandah makes sure the start of the day is wonderful and Shelby in the Press Bar is pretty amazing - remembering my drink every year! I'm grateful for the extraordinary staff.

reviews.title: Wonderful Stay!
reviews.text: We have stayed at many Vegas properties and this was a unique and wonderful experience.  Our trip was for a national volleyball tournament held at the Mandalay Bay Convention Center.  The Four Seasons is an excellent location for anyone attending an event at the Convention Center.  We were extremely happy with the accommodations, service, and private oasis that the Four Seasons provides.

reviews.title: Sensational Experience
reviews.text: Four Seasons is an experience. From the valet we were escorted to the check-in desk and our bags were whisked away.  We arrived at our room to find all our bags had already been delivery and were organized.  On the table there were delicious pears, a glass bottle of water, and a note welcoming us.  The experience I enjoy telling people the most is the first time we left our room and when we returned all charging cables, bags, make-up, etc. had been neatly organized, some even on Four Seasons mats.  It was so cool!  The beds at the Four Seasons will melt all your problems away.  They are super comfy and I seriously feel like I just melt into their beds.  All the amenities at the resort are amazing and never disappoint.  We typically plan a day filled will a trip to the spa followed up with lounging at the private pool.  The Four Seasons upholds is standard of quality throughout the resort, but what really sets them apart is the sensational service!

reviews.title: Amazing stay, Four Seasons Las Vegas
reviews.text: The Four Seasons really does deserve its reputation. From the moment I made reservations staff began reaching out to confirm my preferences for room, arrival and departure, as well as any services I wanted available on arrival. We had meal reservations and pool cabana reserved before even arriving. The food at the Veranda restaurant was outstanding as was the service. Staff were genuinely friendly and happy at the Four Seasons, a welcome change from other hotels were I sometimes feel like I’m bothering the staff. Our room was spotless and well appointed. Housekeeping kept it looking that way throughout our stay. Overall we were very happy and will return.

reviews.title: Best in Vegas by far
reviews.text: Service is the best you’ll find in VEGAS.   At any of the other “luxury “ properties service is saved for the high rollers.I’m not a high roller and prefer the quiet check in and environment of this well known brand.  They have wonderful employees who are trained accordingly.It feels like a smaller hotel; requests aren’t an issue and there aren’t layers of departments to wade through if you happen to need a tea mug or a specific detail to make your stay nicer.  On calling the front desk to inquire about streaming services I was told that they could install an Apple device on the TV for access.  It wasn’t 15 minutes later that a technician came to my room to assist.I’ve had great massage therapists in the spa - up there with all time “bests”.  And I’ve had a lot of treatments at a lot of 5 star properties.I travel California to Utah frequently and stopping there just for a break in the drive feels like an oasis.

reviews.title: An Oasis in Las Vegas
reviews.text: What an oasis in the middle of Las Vegas!  Finally, we have found a hotel where the lobby doesn't smell like cigarette smoke.  The Four Seasons provides a uniquely calm experience that is in the middle of Las Vegas but worlds away from the craziness of the casinos.  We only had one night stay, but I was tempted to stay longer.  The reception was wonderful - efficient and very respectful.  The rooms were spacious, extremely clean and perfect for a good night's sleep.  The restaurant had really, really good food without the hype. We had dinner and breakfast there. Our dinner waiter recommended a wonderful (and not of the top) pinot noir that I am anxious to add to our wine collection.  The breakfast staff were all attentive without making us feel rushed.  My husband used the pool and enjoyed the dip ... though it was, likely necessary, heavily chlorinated.  The valet service was excellent.  I look forward to using this hotel again.

reviews.title: It’s a pass.
reviews.text: I’m surprised at all these amazing reviews. The pool smells like sewer gas. I went 3 days, every day sewer gas. The music at the pool is lacking, like elevator music, I mean it doesn’t have to be club beats but maybe some top 40? No birds of prey at pool so you are surrounded by the rats of the sky. The pool deck must be older bc it will FRY your feet. You cannot walk to the bar or pool steps from your chair wo your feet being burned. This is not the case at other luxury hotels/pools in Vegas. The service at the pool was good & menu was decent. It connects to Mandalay Bay, but like why? The clientele at MB is not what FS guests are looking for. Fair to also note this is a family & pet hotel. Lots of kids in the pool & lots of pets. I don’t mind pets, but when you are at the outdoor restaurants & someone’s dog is peeing in the bush in front of you while you are eating…. Doesn’t scream luxury to me. I stayed in a regular room as I was there for a conference & the shower is TINY. I am not a large bodied person so I can’t imagine how the majority of the guests maneuvered in the shower. So many other great hotels, this wouldn’t even make my top 10 in Vegas.

reviews.title: Four Seasons Hotel.
reviews.text: I’ve stayed at five different Four Seasons in  2024 all over the world. Lots of travel This one certainly isn’t as big but it does what Four Seasons does which is meets your expectations. I was upgraded to a very large suite and the hotel staff you can always tell our professionally trained in hospitality. A great getaway from all the noise in the casinos and the smoke filled rooms. You could take a nice deep breath as soon as you walk into this Four Seasons getting away from the Vegas noise and mess.

reviews.title: Very nice option in Vegas away from the hustle and bustle
reviews.text: We had a great stay at the FS Las Vegas for four nights over Easter this year. Beautiful hotel with very nice rooms good facilities plus the option to use all facilities of the Mandalay bay hotel.We got upgraded to a very nice one-bedroom suite and given all rooms of the FS are on the top floors of the Mandalay Bay, you have great views over the city.Breakfast at Veranda was very nice and with good service.Overall a very pleasant stay and we would surely return next time in Vegas.

reviews.title: Another Extraordinary Stay
reviews.text: During our recent stay at the Four Seasons Las Vegas, we were incredibly impressed with the superior facilities, cleanliness, and service standards. However, it was the exceptional staff at this resort that truly distinguished it within Las Vegas's competitive luxury landscape.The front office staff, particularly Jesus Junez and Curtis Cachero, demonstrated remarkable attentiveness and personalized service. Their warm welcomes and consistent recognition of our past stays greatly enhanced our experience. Drew, the concierge, went above and beyond to accommodate our needs, providing us with complimentary sunglasses to ensure that our time at the pool was maximized. (My mom had forgotten her pair at home). Gamini, the bellman, and Josiah, the security personnel, also displayed exceptional hospitality, further contributing to our overall satisfaction. Salar Alemi's thoughtful welcome gift of chocolate, prunes, and a personal note added a special touch to our arrival, and Jarrod proved to be very helpful as well.In guest relations, Camille Bagnol and Brigitte's efforts in securing a beautiful room and arranging a delightful arrival amenity for our celebratory occasions were truly appreciated. It included a beautiful photo frame, with a developed photo of my mom and I waiting in our room upon our arrival. Wow! Their consistent follow-ups and attention to detail embodied the utmost care and consideration.In addition, Florame Evans of the housekeeping team provided outstanding service, surpassing our expectations by catering meticulously to our specific requirements and curating a memorable turndown experience for us. She always remembered to provide us extra water, and bath salts. Alice Jeikal stands out as our favorite staff member, demonstrating unwavering dedication in assisting us with our accommodation arrangements and orchestrating exceptional in-room services and experiences. She even helped us make dining reservations! Furthermore, Alice made a point of checking in with us at the pool at the end of her work shifts to ensure that our stay was nothing short of remarkable.Peter Kamau and Thomas La Centra arranged for our delightful poolside cabanas, exhibiting exceptional attention to detail in noting and fulfilling our preferences. Thomas remembered our favorite drinks and ensured we had extra poolside amenities sent to us each day (ex: fruit, ice cream cones, flavored waters…). We were truly pampered by the attentive care of these two gentlemen, who were friendly faces we looked forward to seeing each day. Lastly, Zlata, Snjezana, and Jaron further facilitated exceptional poolside experiences for us. We have established a family-like connection with these three, having engaged with them repeatedly over the years. They greeted us warmly each day and upon our departure with hugs and the kindest sentiment, conveying a sense of genuine belonging and comfort. We felt so at home!We extend our heartfelt appreciation to the Four Seasons Las Vegas for providing us with such an extraordinary stay.

reviews.title: Top notch hotel in every sense
reviews.text: This hotel is probably the best hotel if you are a business traveler. The suits are fantastic and the service is exceptional.

reviews.title: Nice Hotel with No Onsite Gambling - Very comfortable
reviews.text: Very comfortable and relaxing stay.  Nice to not have any gambling in the hotel itself.  The complementary spa/steam room use was a highlight.  Excellent service with some of their staff that have worked at the property for many years.  That speaks volumes.

reviews.title: Four Season Part Deux
reviews.text: On the heels of my last visit and previous review,  I was contacted by the Four Seasons Las Vegas director of rooms. I was extended a room upgrade upon my return to Vegas should I choose to stay with them to ameliorate my past experience. It just so happened that I was planning a return, and took them up on the offer. I was provided a king suite, which in addition to the standard bedroom and full bath, consisted of an additional half bath,   a living area and a dining space overlooking a partial strip view.Upon my arrival I was greeted and escorted from the door to check-in and offered water. At check-in  all went smoothly. I booked this stay using Amex FHR, thus I was provided a small box of truffles (from Amex) and a document outlining the benefits associated with my booking. I made use of all benefits, with the exception of : 12pm check in ( I arrived at 3pm), room upgrade (FS was already providing this) and 4pm check out (my flight was an early morning departure.)  I immediately booked a visit to the spa to use the spa credit ( was lovely as always) , and I visited Veranda for Saturday brunch (weather was perfection for outdoor seating) .All in all I would say this visit was a success, I’d hoped to use the pool but simply did not have an opportunity on  this visit. I hope to visit other Four Seasons in the portfolio in future, but as for Las Vegas it may be time to move a bit further down the strip. Mandalay Bay’s casino feels void of people and joy both day and night, which makes it so unpleasant to gamble in and as FS is a “non-gaming hotel” but part of the Mandalay complex, it is the closest.

reviews.title: Luxury at its finest!
reviews.text: The Four Seasons Las Vegas lives up to what you'd expect from a Four Seasons, i.e. - quality, quality, quality along with exceptional customer service. As it's a Four Seasons the quality and exceptional customer service comes with a price. Due to the cost to stay at the Four Seasons Las Vegas this property will not be in everyone's price range.For those who don't know, the Four Seasons Las Vegas is located within the Mandalay Bay. However, the Four Seasons has it's own entrance, it's own pool, it's own spa, it's own restaurants, etc. As a Four Seasons guest you can easily access the Mandalay Bay shops, casino, restaurants and pool. However, Mandalay Bay guests cannot access the Four Season's amenities.If you are in Las Vegas during the Spring/Summer, take advantage of the Four Seasons pool. It's quaint with plenty of lounge chairs and lots of friendly servers who will bring you water, cold fruit on a plate, lunch, cocktails, etc. We had a group of 10 and rented a cabana (not inexpensive but worth it when the cost was divided by 5 couples). On hot days (we were there in mid-May and temps were 100 degrees!) having a cabana with guaranteed shade was well worth the investment. The cabanas come with a flat screen TV (we had golf on), a refrigerator, a small sofa and a table. Plenty of room for people to lounge plus we secured the chairs in front of the cabana making for a very cozy, friendly atmosphere. The pool is 3.5 to 4 feet deep so more for hanging out then playing around. There were a few families at the pool, but mainly couples and groups of friends with no kids.My wife and I treated ourselves to treatments at the Four Seasons Spa. Again, the cost of the treatments will be on the more expensive side and our treatments were very good. The locker room attendants get you settled, the relaxation area before you go into the treatment room are 1st class. The treatments themselves were great with each massage therapist customizing the treatment based on our individual needs.Pro Tip - both the men's and women's locker rooms at the Four Seasons Spa have eucalyptus, wet steam rooms. The steam rooms are available to be used by any Four Season guest, i.e. - you do not need to have a spa appointment to use the rooms. The wet steam rooms are toasty hot and a great way to sweat out any toxins.Lastly, and certainly not least, the customer service at the Four Seasons is amazing. My wife and I are big coffee drinkers. Each room comes with a Nespresso machine with 4 pods of regular coffee and 2 pods of decaf. We asked the front desk for more regular pods of coffee and in less than 5 minutes a bag of pods were delivered to the room.As Four Seasons is within the Mandalay Bay complex you can access Allegiant Stadium (where the Raiders play) through the casino. If you are traveling to Las Vegas for a Raiders game, think about staying at the Four Seasons.In general, if you have the resources, and are traveling to Las Vegas, be sure to consider staying at the Four Seasons as you will enjoy the experience.

reviews.title: The Best EVER
reviews.text: The best staff. Kind. Courteous. They go above and beyond to give you the best experience. Quiet, expertly cleaned rooms and service.

reviews.title: Great time at Four Seasons, Especially Veranda
reviews.text: Everything has been excellent.  Staff have been very helpful.. We had an amazing breakfast this morning at the Veranda.   I had eggs with caviar. Our server was Lauren Myking, great energy and handled all our requests with patience and competence.

reviews.title: Best hotel
reviews.text: Best best best best four seasons in America! The Four Seasons in Vegas is simply exceptional, thanks largely to its incredible staff. During my visit, the team went above and beyond to make everything perfect—from booking the best experiences to getting me into the hottest spots in town. The theater show was a standout, truly the best show in the city. I'm already looking forward to my next trip! Special thanks also to the staff member who helped me find my wallet during a torrential downpour, and to the spa team who accommodated me even though they were fully booked.

reviews.title: Terrible Service when they are busy
reviews.text: terrible service when they are really busy for a conference. Get ready to wait and not get any responses ...I have stayed at so many Four Seasons all over the world. This is by far the worst one. Stay on the strip. This is very upsetting for the Four Seasons brand.

reviews.title: Oasis Of Tasteful Luxury Amid The Vegas Party!
reviews.text: The Four Seasons offers an oasis of tasteful luxury amid the 24/7 party that is Vegas! Occupying the top 5 floors of Mandalay Bay with a "secret" access door to the Mandalay casino floor and restaurants, the Four Season is a discreet retreat from the casino fun. You could stay here and if it wasn't for the stunning views, you would not know you were in Las Vegas. The hotel is typical of Four Seasons five-star standards with excellent staff and facilities. You have a choice of the private pool area, or you can also access the more elaborate pool complex at the Mandalay. If you want a high-quality restaurant without the casino noise and atmosphere, the Four Seasons delivers that with The Veranda. However, there are also excellent casino options next door, especially Michael Mina's Orla which is highly recommended. I heard that Mina may soon open a new restaurant at the Four Seasons, which I suspect will become a destination in itself.

reviews.title: Always the Best Hotel in Las Vegas!
reviews.text: Mils and his staff made another stay perfect as usual. Such high standards from all the staff. Eileen, Solange and Wendy in Press bar are amazing and remember our beverage selection and they treat you like family. Very special place and once you stay it's impossible to stay anywhere else. Top Shelf service, food, drinks and rooms. Thanks again to Mils for such a special touch!

reviews.title: Vile!
reviews.text: Just vile! the hotel is on the top floors of the Mandalay Bay (probably much cheaper) - it smells like a building that has been on fire, a nasty burnt smell on the 38th floor.Rooms weren't ready at check in. Rooms are tired. They website is very good and suggests the hotel is stylish. In my opinion, it is very unpleasant. The service is average at best. Never again for us. It is a weird hotel. No thank you.

reviews.title: Welcome To Fabulous Four Seasons Vegas
reviews.text: This hotel has become our home away from home when we attend business conferences in Las Vegas. We have stayed here probably close to 20 times in 20 years, yes, it is that good. First and foremost, the hotel itself does not play host to a casino. So if you want to stay away from that aspect of Vegas, you’re  looking for something quieter and very upscale, or traveling with younger members of your family, this is a huge advantage. Should you want to visit a casino, the large, and very busy casino for Mandalay Bay is less than a 2 minute walk from the Four Seasons which is housed in the same complex. Some of the constant highlights of our stays over the years include the excellent attention and care given to us by the house keeping staff and also the concierge. By far some of the best in the industry. Additionally, we have been greeted by the pool staff, many of the same staff members of the pool have been there for decades, and they have basically watched our daughter go from toddler to adult. It’s always incredible to us, each visit, that they truly remember us! The rooms are kept up beautifully and offer everything you would expect of a Four Sesaons. Decor is lovely. On property dining is excellent, inclusive of The Verandah for a quicker, excellent meal, room service and the lobby coffee bar as well as cocktail lounge. Overall, if you are looking to not be “just another number” at a mega resort in Vegas and seeking actual luxury, Four Seasons is the place!

reviews.title: Another great stay at the Four Seasons Las Vegas
reviews.text: Another excellent stay at the Four Seasons Las Vegas which sits atop Mandalay Bay on several floors. Highlights:*Amazing views from every room - especially during the day.*Excellent service all around - very attentive*Clean, modern and fresh guest rooms*Quiet rooms - can't hear anyone or anything around you!*fast elevators from FS lobby to guest rooms, don't have to wait long*easy secured access to/from Mandalay Bay lobby and casino floors*easy to valet or get rideshare from lobby area*food and convenience shopping within Four Seasons confine *easy access to the outside recreation area from the FS lobby*dog friendly!

reviews.title: A peaceful oasis!
reviews.text: My husband and I lived every minute of our stay at the Four Seasons The room was beautiful and impeccably cleaned twice a day.   The entire staff was very gracious and genuine about being helpful.  We hope to return to this peaceful oasis in Las Vegas!

reviews.title: Seasons Change
reviews.text: I presented to the 4S lobby to check in and leave my bags. While I waited, I observed various check-in processes underway. One guest was being asked her preferred room temperature and was then escorted to the guest elevators. Another was given water, while yet others were provided champagne. My room was not yet ready, so l would have to return later that afternoon. l received a text when the room was ready, retrieved my keys (still offered no refreshments) or even guidance to the guest elevators. Additional note: there is a casino level door with access to guest room elevators. I wish they would have mentioned this at check in, it will save you about a miles walk and time. It is not well marked.General stay:I was there on business with a colleague/friend with whom I'd planned to share a room. We were provided a strip view room, but with only  a single bed. Not ideal to have to share a bed, but we made it work.The accommodation itself was nice, the room was updated but the bathroom did not appear to be. I appreciate that a lot of hotels now have refillable bathing products vs. single use ; I found these products a bit drying, but they worked for my companion. The shower was small but the water pressure was great!Twice daily housekeeping was such a treat. Our towels were kept clean, our Nespresso stocked and evening bedside waters were much appreciated. Little touches like cord organizers for our charging cables, or leaving an eyeglass cleaning cloth with my sunglasses was thoughtful.We ordered room service one early evening. It was so nice to see that they still offer traditional room service with the dining cart, cloche covered bites and real cutlery and tableware. As opposed to the takeout bags and containers from other hotels.We used the spa services, l've reviewed that separately. As a guest, you have access to the steam room- I wish someone would have told us that in advance as I thought we only had gym access.Due to convenience, we went to Veranda for 3 consecutive breakfasts. Service was good; food was decent.My only major disappointments come from the differences in the check-in treatment of each guest and being addressed by the wrong name multiple times by multiple different staff. Whether it was in person at the spa, by housekeeping, by room service, at Vernada (one server got it right, I believe her name was May) and the front desk. I even messaged them to make sure I was a listed guest for billing reasons. They again, addressed me by my companions name in that message exchange despite me messaging them from my account, everything being on my card and the room booked in my name.If an organization insists on the “personal touch” of addressing guests by name, make sure you're using the right one. Otherwise, it feels halfhearted and borderline disrespectful.Would I stay again? Maybe, but with so many options in Las Vegas there may be better choices out there where I am not made to feel less than, which does not support The Golden Rule.

reviews.title: Elegant, Superior Service, Non-Smoking
reviews.text: we had the best time staying at the four seasons Las Vegas. From beginning to end, the service was impeccable. We enjoyed our food in our room and the restaurant, and also we had wonderful experiences at the spa. we also utilized the gym while we were there. we will be staying there again. Officialhilaryroberts

reviews.title: I've been at better Four Seasons.
reviews.text: Room rather small. Shower like a phone booth. Concierge would not call for a taxi the following morning for ourdeparture. . Not sure why. Very expensive food options. On the good side, views of the strip were awesome from our room.  We were here for a funeral.

reviews.title: A Tranquil Oasis in the Midst of a City
reviews.text: My husband and I recently stayed at the Four Seasons in Las Vegas and couldn't have been happier with our choice. As soon as we stepped into the hotel we felt calm (no casino and smoke free) and welcomed. We were warmly greeted by Alice and Alessa, who not only went above and beyond with assigning us a quiet room but also gave us an upgrade as well. Not only was our room spacious, it was well appointed as well, complete with the Four Seasons signature comfortable bed. For the rest of our stay we were treated with the upmost kindness by the entire team, from Javiar our server at breakfast, Amy my spa therapist and Curtis at the Bell Hop who really took the time to get to know us. Thank you and we'll definitely be back on our next visit to Vegas.

reviews.title: Exceptional facility and service
reviews.text: Highly recommend this resort. Staff are gracious and hospitable, rooms very comfortable and spa well appointed and attended. Food and service at Veranda and Press are excellent. Prices can be exorbitant but stay was impeccable.

reviews.title: Excellent hotel, can't wait to return!
reviews.text: We had a wonderful stay 3-night stay at the Four Seasons Las Vegas right after Christmas. The hotel is truly 5-star, with comfortable rooms, a beautiful lobby, and great service. This is a non-smoking and non-gambling hotel, so it smells amazing (unlike some other hotels on the strip) and isn't hectic. If you do want to gamble, it's connected to the Mandalay Bay so you can access everything there.Service was wonderful; we arrived after a hellish drive in holiday traffic 4 hours late and starving. They got us seated at the bar right after check-in and we had a delicious cocktail and meal within 30 minutes.  Later on, my husband slammed his finger in a car door and the bar staff and front desk staff were super helpful in getting him iced up so he could minimize swelling. The next morning they checked in on him--it was totally unnecessary but really sweet and appreciated.The only thing to note is that is is quite far south on the Strip. This is great for access to things outside of the Strip, but something to keep in mind if you have activities planned farther up the Strip. Also, breakfast was great but the wait can get long!

reviews.title: Too Hot.  Too long. Uncomfortable
reviews.text: Too Warm.  No AccommodationThe staff is mostly excellent and friendly.  The room is large and bed was comfortable The room was too HOT and they don’t allow you to adjust the temperature lower. I called three times in two separate days.  They first told me they would adjust because they control the temps.  Then they sent someone to the room.  Then they said they would adjust.  Over 4 days, it never happened.  I woke up in a pool of sweat.  So my sleep was disrupted throughout my 3 night stay.  Very disappointed with a luxury hotel in a brand that prides itself on customer service. My shower head was detached from the wall.  You’d expect proper maintenance.  The bathroom door would not stay open without a   Prop placed in front of it  I think 4 seasons can do better and they should

reviews.title: Lovely, Calm hotel in LV
reviews.text: Having NO Casino makes this hotel very desirable. We stayed there for a big birthday celebration. We were met at check in with champagne (real not a sparkler). The staff is very knowledgable and friendly. The location is away from the LV craziness.
