reviews.text: Great location if attending a tradeshow at Mandela’s Bay. Excellent service and rooms. Staff are always accommodating and with no gambling in lobby it is a nice reprove from the tropical Las Vegas scene.

reviews.title: An unfortunate set of circumstances
reviews.text: Unfortunately, not all Four Seasons are the same. From arrival, thanks to a very impatient valet named Chris... we were treated with respect by only Alayna at registration. Management actually deceived us with a reservation switch to Mandalay Bay? Why would they do that? The transparency was sadly inappropriate. Anyhow, noted for the future. So many other choices!

reviews.title: Wonderful accommodations
reviews.text: Very nice place to stay. Unfortunately all the pot & cigarrette smoking on the streets tainted our experience. My biggest complaint is that is overpriced. We stay at gorgeous Sqauw Creek resort for much less. But the hotel itself was actually a haven from that. Prompt room service. Tasty food at the Veranda. And Cafe Umbria was a nice hang out any time of the day. Bath robes were a little small and the room fridge had not extra space for personal items. But the staff was courteous and attentive.

reviews.title: Fantastic, awesome, terrific - are 3 words for this hotel
reviews.text: I have traveled to so many countries and stayed in so many hotels.. but this place tops my list and is one of the best places to stay. Amazing plush rooms, fantastic bathrooms, neat and tidy linen and ‘out of the world’ service.. I can go on and on and on. They would clean, tidy up and replenish your room even if you step out for 3rd time on the same day. Totally loved the whole experience. Food was amazing to add! Four seasons is on the strip itself and must must must stay kind of place!

reviews.title: Great Hotel if You're Looking for Peace and Quiet
reviews.text: It's a nice retreat from the hustle and bustle of Vegas, but you're close enough if you want to partake in that. The room was a bit small for a typical Four Seasons room, but very nicely decorated and extremely comfortable. Decent view, too. The food was probably the best I've had at a Four Seasons, so def high-five on that. Worth the price.

reviews.title: Can't Stay Anywhere Else Now
reviews.text: This was my third trip to Vegas and now, I can't stay anywhere else. Top notch service, beautiful room and overall experience. Staff remembered by name and it smelled fresh and good wherever you go. I liked having security to check you into the elevator as well. Everywhere in Vegas seems to smell like smoke and feel cheap - except here. The Veranda restaurant had great food and a lively and bright atmosphere - perfect for meeting with colleagues or friends.

reviews.title: Four Seasons Las Vegas
reviews.text: The best staff! From the moment I arrived to moment I departed, everyone was polite, friendly and accommodating. The hotel itself is a welcome quiet oasis from the loud and bright casinos. The rooms are comfortable and spotless and the views are spectacular. The food was delicious and plenty. I highly recommend the Four Seasons Las Vegas.

reviews.title: Friendly service in a Luxury Hotel
reviews.text: I had never stayed at the Four Seasons in Las Vegas and it turned out to be a 5 star experience.  The hotel is small and intimate with no casino ( one adjacent in the Mandalay Bay) and it made for a peaceful and elegant respite.  The hotel is beautiful and immaculate.

reviews.title: Great visit
reviews.text: This hotel was very clean, staff were great, and they provided a 5 star experience. From arrival to departure, I was greeted by all the staff I would pass. They couldn't have been more pleasant in my opinion.

reviews.title: In Vegas for golf
reviews.text: My brothers and I ate lunch at the Four Seasons while in Vegas on a golf trip. It was a Sunday, so they had a brunch going that looked excellent, though a little pricey at $42. They also allowed ordering off the breakfast or lunch menus. We all ordered off the lunch menu. We had shrimp tacos, a steak sandwich (which was served with dill pickle fries) and a shrimp/scallop/pasta dish. Two of us had tap beers and the third had a glass of wine. Service was very attentive, the food was tasty, portions were generous and the setting was quite nice. The bill was $144, so you are paying a premium for what you get. If cost is not a concern, you will enjoy the Four Season.

reviews.title: Quiet, Sophisicated Hotel
reviews.text: This hotel is for the discriminating guest who wishes to have a smoke free envirnoment as well as no Casino inhouse  With that said, there is direct access off the elevator to the Casino at the neighboring hotel.  You cant access the Casino easily and back into the hotel with a Four Season Hotel key.   Love the security at the hotel elevator.  Dining for breakfast, lunch and dinner is marevlous.  The bedding is luxerious.  THE place to stay in Las Vegas.

reviews.title: Friendly Staff, Beautiful Lobby “pros and cons”
reviews.text: We stayed in a strip view upgrade Pros- I Can’t say it enough but the staff is super friendly, something about a smile at every corner makes you feel great. - Beautifully Decorated Lobby - Bed and Sheets were amazing, clean, comfortable and the bed was wow. - Bathroom toiletries amazing wouldn’t expect any less from the Four Seasons. Although the room was nice I struggled with giving this property anything better than Average. With past experiences staying at Four Seasons properties this was a very average stay. Cons- Room upkeep from outlets coming out of the wall, burnout lighting in the bathroom to what looked like warped ceiling with cracks.- Rooms were much smaller than expected - Noise level from the hall in the morning time was a bit ridiculous. Typically in the higher end vegas hotels they have a way of controlling those types of noise levels so guests can enjoy a good nights sleep. - Turn down services was not the best, all of our trash was still left in the room, it only looks like they came in to do the bed. Staying at other high end rooms on the strip, the trash is taken out, room is once again straighten up and the bed is ready for the guest to come back and sleep. - A late checkout was never offered I come to find out from checking out via the tv that I could have been offered a 3pm late check out which would have been very helpful to know the night prior. Final thought: although I love the brand this property is definitely a skip for the next time and truly can not recommend if you are expecting a luxurious stay on the strip.

reviews.title: Customer service- best in industry.
reviews.text: Wow.  Service that is on-par with top luxury cruise lines.  Attuned service.  Unobtrusive housekeeping staff that is available throughout the day.  Pristine and clean.  Cannot put a price on being treated well... A++++

reviews.title: Amazing service, comfortable bedrooms, an oasis of calm
reviews.text: The hotel truly lives up to the Four Seasons brand, it offers courteous service, great amenities and a sense of peace and calm. The best place to stay in Las Vegas if your goal is luxury. We stayed at this hotel several times over the years and it never disappoints!

reviews.title: Hidden Gem
reviews.text: This is the best place to get away from the Vegas crazy and recharge so you can hit it hard again weather its work or pleasure. I really love coming here when I'm there for conference and also good for couples my wife absolutely loves it.

reviews.title: An Oasis on the Strip
reviews.text: We were in town to celebrate the ending of the school term with our two boys (teen and tween).  They loved being in the middle of it all but away from the chaos, smoke and crowds of the other hotels.  The staff was extraordinary.  The concierge team helped plan a range of activities and meals and had spot on suggestions. I am sure all the spa services are excellent but if you are able to get a message with Elizabeth, it will be outstanding. The valet team was super friendly but professional and very focused on safety --always confirming the Uber license plate or the valet ticket.  The restaurant service was very on point. The rooms are typical (very nice) Four Seasons city rooms but the staff at every turn made the visit very special.

reviews.title: An Oasis in the Desert
reviews.text: I booked at the Four Seasons for a conference, but my husband and I tacked on time to celebrate our first anniversary. The hotel accommodated both extraordinarily well, proving as a quiet oasis for our networking among the jangling casino in Mandalay Bay, and also a romantic escape at the edge of the strip. The rooms are extremely comfortable and feel plush, and the attention to detail is what undoubtedly makes Four Seasons a coveted accommodation. The wire cords and the lens cloths are unexpected extras (at least for anyone not used to staying in a luxury hotel). We were also sent a lovely plate of goodies on the final night wishing us a happy anniversary. Staff are friendly and service is anticipatory. I felt an effort on behalf of everyone to make each guest feel VIP. I would love to come back when the weather is a bit warmer to enjoy the pool area, but otherwise nothing at all was lacking from this short trip. Our views of the strip were exciting, but being one step removed from the Vegas bustle at the end of the day made for the relaxing retreat we were hoping for.

reviews.title: Here on business and very disappointed!!!! Buyer Beware!!!!
reviews.text: We are here on business. Very nice service upon check in but was completely caught by surprise when we were told due to a group in house they could not accommodate our request for a king bed. They offered us two double beds which we declined. We were them told they have a 1 bedroom suite for an up charge which we declined then told us they have a suite with king bed for an up charge which we declined. Then told they had a king in the same type of room with a view of the strip with a king bed for an upcharge!!!! We agreed to the same room with king and strip view rather then settle for 2 double beds.  We have stayed in many hotels including four seasons. We have never had an experience like this with trying to get a king bed without an upcharge. Normally hotels will upgrade you if they can not accommodate your request? Not this one.  Very dissappointed with this up sell and would think twice about coming back for business or pleasure!Not the standard we would expect from this type of property compared to past experiences.

reviews.title: Recent Stay
reviews.text: Everything was as expected for a Four Seasons experience.   I particularly like the private check in and out without having to walk through a casino.  Stayed at this location several times and never had any disappointment of any type.  Nice job folks!

reviews.title: Oasis on the Strip
reviews.text: We booked this hotel as we wanted a non gaming and non smoking hotel to get some R&R from the chaos of Las Vegas. A really good choice, location is at the end of the strip but if you want somewhere to go back to and get some peace and quiet it’s perfect. Easy to get around by taxi, tram or walking. If you want a casino it’s next door via a connecting door. Staff really friendly and helpful. Press is a lovely coffee bar and has breakfast items available from 530am.

reviews.title: If there were 6 stars they would get the rating from me
reviews.text: This hotel is out of this world! Faultless, high luxury, totally fantastic! I know it sounds over the top but ... it’s true! Porters are very welcoming and helpful, receptionists and concierges the same: nothing is too much trouble, you are really made feel special and valued by all staff. Reception and common areas are extremely elegant and the bedrooms ... are to die for! Great views (the Four Seasons is located on the top floors of the Mandalay Bay/ separate entrance) extremely spacious exquisitely decorated rooms, super comfortable beds, enormous elegant bathroom, mega huge TV, high speed WiFi ... perfection taken to the finest degree. The price isn’t modest but it is totally justified, every cent of it. I stayed two nights and wish I could stay forever. Highly recommend to others!

reviews.title: World class staff and a great non-gaming experience
reviews.text: I have zero complaints with the hotel amenities and none with the staff. The entire stay was great with respect to the accommodations.  They have earned my recommendation and we will be back again soon.

reviews.title: Great stay at the end of the strip
reviews.text: The four seasons occupies a few floors of the mandalay bay building at the end of the strip. Rooms have a great view and service is excellent. This was one one of the nicer hotels we have stayed in recently with excellent pillows and a bed so comfy that we didn’t want to leave it. Super nice bathroom too.

reviews.title: Second to none
reviews.text: Every Four Seasons always confirms my choise is right. Perfect location and atmosphere with best service. Whenever I stay at Four Seasons, it makes me comfortable and pride of being a guest of hotel. Four Seasons know what "Customer" meas.

reviews.title: Peace
reviews.text: In a busy, even hectic place like Las Vegas it was a blessing to go back to the calm and welcoming atmosphere at the Four Seasons. We had prepaid for 4 nights in a “lakeview” room at the Bellagio, but the quality of the room (extremely worn) the service and lack of amenities in the room (no bathrobe or slippers) not functioning heating caused us to forfeit 3 nights and escape to the bliss at Four Seasons. We felt like we had moved from Hell to Heaven.

reviews.title: Oasis of calm
reviews.text: I enjoyed a great holiday stay at the Four Seasons Las Vegas.  While the hotel itself is on the top floors of the Mandalay Bay tower, it has its own reception and lobby that doesn’t make you go through a casino to get to the rooms / reception.  The rooms were well appointed with really terrific strip views.  We enjoyed breakfast each day at the Veranda restaurant, the choices were extensive and quite delicious.  The hotel also had some fun, seasonal treats, such as hot cider and hot chocolate.  This was definitely the right spot for our family trip.

reviews.title: Mixed bag
reviews.text: Not really an independent hotel but a small section (some floors) of the Mandala bay.Independent lobby and a few restaurants. Quieter than most (no casino in lobby or adjacent).Nice classical rooms.Mediocre restaurant offer, but mandala bay offers more choice so not too big an issue.Expensive.Friendly staff in reception, not so much at the bar (Press).

reviews.title: Vegas New Years Eve
reviews.text: Last minute trip to see Lady Gaga Jazz and Piano and celebrate New Years in Vegas with our adult children. . Four Seasons staff made everything happen in a very short time frame-it was perfect. Exceptional Service by all Four Seasons Staff.  The Four Seasons is a quiet oasis to escape the excitement and energy of a Vegas stay especially on New Years.  Loved every minute of our stay with the Four Seasons.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: I booked the room for a business associate.  A diva indeed.  That is why I selected the Four Seasons. I called 3 times prior to her arrival to make sure everything would be perfect ordering a basket, her favorite tea, hotel car pick-up and an early check-in.  But upon her arrival, she claimed not to have a car for incidentals.  Well instead of calling me, (my phone number and credit card on the room), they made her sit in the lobby and sit, and sit.  They would not let her in the paid room.  But the time I was contacted, they refused to use the card which I reserved the room and made me drive to the hotel to show the card.  I know she is a pain, but the Four Season handled this BADLY. Luckily I live in Vegas and could go to the hotel or I guess she would have been in the lobby all night.  BOO...Bad job Four Seasons!

reviews.title: Disappointing stay
reviews.text: I had high expectations for this hotel and was there  for a business event my company was running  at the four seasons Vegas. The first thing that was annoying was finding my way around. Sometimes I would wind up at the adjoining hotel just by going up the wrong stairway or from the elevator. It was very very confusing  to get around. The lighting in the rooms are very dim and room in general was outdated. I did like the food so that was the only redeeming quality for this hotel.

reviews.title: 3 Stay Stay After Christmas
reviews.text: Stayed here for three days right after Christmas as part of a family reunion type of weekend.The room and bed were very comfortable - the shower & bathroom very spacious - and the towels and robe more than adequate. Had drinks at the bar one night and ordered appetizers - received prompt and attentive service as well as at the little coffee area right in the lobby area.Family ate at the restaurant upon arrival to use up a food credit - nice meal although the service was just a little bit slow.This is a very nice hotel with the small but nicely appointed fitness area.

reviews.title: A most pleasant stay.
reviews.text: Fabulous service, beautiful guest rooms, comfortable beds.  Only drawback was lack of off-season swimming pool on facility.  Pool was offered at Mandalay Bay, but seemed a bit inconvenient.  Overall, we would highly recommend this facility.

reviews.title: GREAT HOTEL BUT SLOW ROOM SERVICE
reviews.text: Stayed here a few times and love it!  Quiet, great room, amazing bed, COLD Air Conditioner...The only complaint is the In-Room Dining is SO SLOW it's agonizing!  Plan ahead and even if you want a snack, prepare to wait an hour!

reviews.title: I had high expectations, but the Four Seasons exceeded them
reviews.text: We had a great stay at the hotel. I have stayed at many other hotels on the strip, but this was my first time at the Four Seasons. Our room was on the 37th floor and the views of the strip were great. The rooms were nice and housekeeping was outstanding. Breakfast was top notch—I think the buffet is only available on the weekends.  The doughnuts were very good. There is no casino in the hotel but there is a Four Seasons elevator that can take you to the Mandalay Bay casino.  It was very easy to get to the casino. If you have AMEX Platinum, I recommend booking the hotel through AMEX Fine Hotels & Resorts.

reviews.title: The only hotel....
reviews.text: ….in all Vegas, apparently, that has no gambling, the Four Seasons still presents a welcoming face without the cynicism of being charming to paying punters. As the rooms are on the top floors you are guaranteed a good view and I recommend the side that overlooks the airport, which is dangerously – in a good way – close. The staff, however, need a bit of training. I was very rudely treaded at breakfast by a snotty little hostess who had all the charm of a rattlesnake and none of the frisson of excitement. Once bitten, twice shy and I won’t be going again.

reviews.title: It all depends on what you are looking for
reviews.text: The hotel is the top floors of the Mandalay Bay so you are entering through a seperate entrance.  I love that the hotel is quiet and not all of the noise from a casino.  The security is very tight.  There is one to two security guards who stand at the elevator to avoid people following guest to their room.  You do need a key to get up the elevator.  Our room was rather large, the beds fantastic and very quiet.The negative is that you will need to taxi to most places due to the distance from the other hotels/casinos.  My boyfriend and I decided we were stay somewhere more central next time such as the Winn. They have hot complimentary donuts in the lobby that are to die for!   The restaurant for lunch was not great and I did not eat my food.   Hotel staff was excellent.  It is cheaper to uber/lyft to other casinos than taxi.

reviews.title: Another amazing stay
reviews.text: For anyone looking for an amazing hotel in Vegas without a casino, this is your best and only option. Everything about it is amazing. Great location, friendly staff, spotlessly clean hotel, large rooms, fantastic service. There is simply no better option. If we come back to Vegas, this is the only place we would stay.

reviews.title: New Year stay
reviews.text: I love the Four Seasons. I highly recommend it. We stayed for the New Year celebration and it’s a beautiful hotel with an excellent service. It’s away from the craziness of the casinos and it’s clean and quiet and absolutely amazing. You get the room cleaning twice a day and the staff is always attentive and there to help. We received a nice surprise on December 31 and it was a chocolate sculpture. That was very sweet. Their brunches are excellent too :).

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: This is one of the best hotels in Vegas.  It is separate from the casino which gives it a sense of calm.  The staff is amazing and helpful and rooms contemporary and very comfortable.  This is my favorite place in Vegas to stay.

reviews.title: “Gambler’s hideaway
reviews.text: We think anybody who works in service or cherishes service should stay at Four Seasons Hotel Las Vegas!The really LIVE service and are a stellar model for service. At such a place you get a notion of the true meaning of PARADISE.

reviews.title: First Time Vegas
reviews.text: I always must travel for a work conference, and this year was in Vegas. My first time, so I did not know much about city. 4Seasons was on southern most point of city. Major pluses were: near convention center, sushi options were numerous, concierge was one of the best I have ever worked with, and everything was super clean. I would say if you are a budget traveler, the whole city is going to be a challenge. 4Seasons was not the cheapest option, but I would definitely stay there again.

reviews.title: The best hotel in Vegas
reviews.text: The Four Seasons Hotel Las Vegas offers their usual luxury accommodations and fantastic service and it is nice to be away from the madness, smoke and noises of the casinos.  Although physically part of the Mandalay Bay Resort, the Four Seasons has its own porte-cochere entry as well as a restricted entry to the central lobby of the Mandalay Bay. One feels very safe with all the personnel on duty and everyone from the doorman to the housekeepers are cordial and welcoming. You will get a good night's rest and the walls are so thick and insulated that you will not hear your neighbors at all. Web check-in makes the process go faster and checkout was a breeze.

reviews.title: Ppe-Christmas stay
reviews.text: Beautiful, quite Las Vegas Hotel, It was nice to not be part of the "herd" in other Las Vegas resorts.Staff was very friendlyand  personable and the concierge department helped us to find shows and dinners that were great experiences. Best , quiet sleep ever in a Vegas hotel. Overall loved it and would definitely stay here again. In the past, my wife and I would always choose a different vegas resort to experience.. From now on, I will sleep here and visit the others during the day. This was our  7th different resort in the last  few years. Again Highly Recommend

reviews.title: Traveling with family, I won't stay anywhere else again!
reviews.text: The service is fantastic and the rooms are perfect, as are most Four Seasons properties, but the one reason I will be back again and again is that I won't be forced to walk through a casino filled with the smell of smoke!

reviews.title: Dining
reviews.text: Press bar has a good service and happy hour disappointing to see that verandah is no longer available for dinner or bar service. Overall the happy prices are great but not really clear what is on happy hour and what is not.

reviews.title: Service, Comfort & Luxury
reviews.text: This was our first visit to this property and we always stay in Five Star hotels when we visit Las Vegas.  I am in love with the Four Seasons in Las Vegas!  This is my new favorite property.  We will be returning - no questions asked!  From the moment that we arrived and the concierge escorted us to the check-in desk to the moment that we departed; the service was world-class.  I am very impressed with this hotel.  The rooms were very comfortable and we got a good night's rest.  Our view of the strip was amazing.  We did not have any noise issues and all of the amenities (gym, spa, etc...) were pure luxury.  This hotel ranks higher than the Mandarin Oriental (currently Waldorf Astoria) which used to be in Vegas - in my personal experience.

reviews.title: Property has devalued.
reviews.text: I have been coming to this property since 1999 whenever I had occasion to visit Las Vegas either for business or pleasure, which tends now to be semi-annual, whereas in the past was more frequent. I have consistently stayed at the Four Seasons, for many reasons, not the least of which is the seclusion one can find whilst having ready access to Mandalay Bay and the Strip. The property is still well maintained and the facilities are good, however, certain changes have really devalued its appeal. The restaurant, Veranda is now no longer open for evening dining, which is a real shame as it was a) very good and b) leaves you with the sole option of Charlie Palmer which is both overpriced and over hyped. Worse yet, the Veranda bar is closed and one’s only option is the lobby bar which is thoroughly bereft of atmosphere, comfort and value for money. Pleasant serving staff, but just doesn’t cut it, especially with one particular Chardonnay (not my tipple) costing $37!They have recently instituted a “resort fee” of $39 per night. I have a particular dislike of these fees and wish they would simply build it into the rate. Nevertheless, it is made all the more irksome when all the pool, hot tub, outdoor facilities are closed and not available. Another example of “nickel and diming”.Room service food quality was excellent, albeit an additional 27% is added to the food cost for in-room, which is somewhat excessive in my view. So, sad to say this will no longer be a “go to” property, albeit if you are a Raiders fan, it’s going to be very convenient.

reviews.title: Oasis of calm and luxury in whirlpool Las Vegas
reviews.text: Very friendly staff here and the quality of rooms and food is high; a separate hotel section in the Mandala Bay resort. Concierge and Valet VERY helpful.  Only minor improvements could be speed of service and opening the hotel bar past 11pm (not that there aren't many other bars around).  A very pleasurable hotel experience.

reviews.title: Four Seasons Consistently Impresses
reviews.text: I travel to Las Vegas monthly for work and the staff and hotel at the Four Seasons is the best place I have stayed.  I have been to all the hotels on the Strip but there is no equal in service, attention to detail and physical space.  Really pays to be a repeat customer there.  Highly recommend if you can get in.

reviews.title: Fantastic Experience
reviews.text: I stayed at the Four Seasons for two nights as part of a work trip. I was traveling alone so I appreciated the great service and apparent security that the hotel has. I was greeted kindly upon arrival and was able to check in easily without a wait. On my way to the rental car center, the heel popped off my shoe. The front desk clerk walked me over to the concierge, who was able to arrange for a service to pick up my shoe, repair it and return it to the hotel the same day. What a life saver! The fee for the service was not bad at all. The hotel is connected to Mandalay Bay by elevator and a door that is accessed with a room key. The elevators also are accessible only with a room key. While the Four Seasons itself is quiet and upscale, a short walk can bring you to the chaos of the Mandalay Bay casino and all its bars and restaurants.My room on the 38th floor was a decent size -- not huge by Vegas standards, but certainly big enough. More important, it was immaculately clean and well-insulated. My room faced south toward the airport, and I barely heard the planes.The fitness center is accessible without an extra fee and is a good size with everything you might want or need during your stay.Overall, I found the hotel staff to be friendly and really interested in providing top quality service. I moved the Aria for a girls' trip that followed my work trip, and I love that hotel. But the personal and genuine service at the Four Seasons was just a step above. I was really happy with my stay and would definitely stay here again on a business trip.

reviews.title: Feel at Home
reviews.text: My wife and I have stayed in Las Vegas many times and always come back to the Four Seasons because the staff there make us feel so welcome and comfortable.  The hotel is easy to navigate, and the food is exceptional.  You can't go wrong with the Four Seasons.

reviews.title: Las Vegas 50 th Birthday
reviews.text: Perfect weekend get away for my husband 's birthday. Chocolate covered strawberries amazing. Pool was a perfect 87 degrees F even though the temperature outside was in the 40s. Spa and 80 minute massage was perfect. High quality food at the breakfast buffet. Service impeccable. Can not wait to return. Will only stay at the Four Seasons in the future when visiting Las Vegas.

reviews.title: Plush
reviews.text: We were able to get a discounted rate for a suite at the Four Seasons Las Vegas (Mandalay) and we were not disappointed. It was size of 2 standard rooms seamlessly married together to create a great personal space. One side was was the sleeping quarters with a sleeping area and full bathroom. The other side was a living room with desk and wet bar AND a separate water closet... great for chili and beer night gentleman..... I'm sure the wife appreciated it.Staff was on point the whole trip. Everyone was friendly and welcoming. Not a grumpy buzz killer in the bunch. The room staff made sure we returned to a clean and restocked room every evening. Didn't even have to think about it.We usually stay in the Venetian/Caesars part of the strip but a work conference had us on this side. It was a great surprise.

reviews.title: Classy experience
reviews.text: Located on the Mandalay Bay property this hotel has direct access to the Las Vegas Strip and immediately north of the Mandalay Bay Convention Center.  High quality service begins at valet. Inside currently a large Christmas tree in the lobby.

reviews.title: Truely, luxury  with a smile
reviews.text: Your first impression of the Four Seasons is when you arrive, an the staff look at a tag on your luggage and great you by name. How great is that. Everyone wants to help make your stay special, and it is. They walk you to your room and make sure that everything is what you expected, PERFECT! Its the little touches that make this hotel special, as when I watch TV I need distance glasses, so I leave them on the bed table, and when I return there is a Four Seasons micro-cloth to clean them! And then there are the many wires that one uses to stay in touch with the world and the four seasons has a small velcrotape that they use to consolidate your cords so they don't hang all over the desk. Its the small things that make you come back, with a smile!

reviews.title: New Vegas Favorite
reviews.text: Currently, my favorite hotel on the strip. I like that the lobby and hotel area are compartmentalized from the Mandalay Bay Resort & Casino and that it gives you some quiet if you want it. Great customer service and well-maintained like you would expect from FS properties. Mini-bar is expensive but not obscene like other strip hotels. Solid breakfast buffet. For personal travel, definitely recommend booking through the AMEX Fine Hotels & Resorts program as they offer some great perks (complimentary breakfast, spa credit, and 4pm checkout).

reviews.title: November Trip
reviews.text: First trip to Vegas in a November. Weather was nice, wish it was warmer for pool weather but still enjoyable. This was at the end of November so we were able to see some Christmas decorations up in various hotels.

reviews.title: Beautiful Setting & Nice Gym
reviews.text: Currently staying here for a week.  The property has a beautiful elegant and intimate setting. The service is outstanding everywhere.  The staff has excellent service training and really make the guests feel special.  I am loving it here.

reviews.title: Perfection!
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed at the Four Seasons for a three night retreat for our Honeymoon and his Birthday. My husband is on life support which requires a great deal of equipment and care. We trusted the Four Seasons as our first time traveling since his condition and they truly outdid themselves. We had to have many cases of equipment shipped to the Hotel prior to arrival and a table set up in our room in advanced for the equipment. This was done prior to arrival and the Hotel even draped the table so that it would not take away from the Hotel room beautiful decor. The entire staff was the best and we have stayed at many Four Seasons from Chicago to Paris. They made us feel like royalty and the service was outstanding. Housekeeping is amazing and the rooms are luxurious and well appointed. Could not have had a better trip and we can now travel with knowing the Four Seasons will take care of our special medical circumstances.

reviews.title: Wonderful escape
reviews.text: We particularly wanted a non-gaming hotel for a more relaxing experience.  This hotel is located on the top few floors of the Mandalay Bay and has its own entrance and elevators.   We were able to walk (and tram, and Uber) and enjoy all the Strip has to offer, but have a quieter oasis to relax in. Great spa and restaurant.  Wonderful rooms and amenities. It has exceeded our expectations and we will stay here on future visits.

reviews.title: Vegas gem
reviews.text: I stayed here before and they upgraded me to a suite so this time is a bit of a letdown. The room was comfortable but sort of small in the bathroom and shower were nice. Overall it was a comfortable stay but I think next time I would go to one of the other Hotels that offers larger rooms.

reviews.title: A haven in Vegas
reviews.text: This hotel is a gem in Las Vegas - no casino to walk through to get to your room, stylish decoration and peaceful pool area. If you want a place away from the chaos, this is the place. The food and drink is excellent (although not cheap) and rooms spacious. I stayed for a weekend to run the half marathon and got a tray of flapjacks and chocolate in my room with a good luck message day before the run - this gives you an idea of the level of service.

reviews.title: Birthday trip to Vegas
reviews.text: I had a wonderful stay at this property for my boyfriend’s birthday. It’s a beautiful, classy hotel that is not overwhelmingly huge like most of the casino hotels — but provides access to all of that, if you want it. The level of customer service was great. I was greeted by name everywhere and the concierge (Drew) helped put together a full itinerary of fun date nights with cocktails (64th floor Strip views) and dinner reservations. I can’t wait to come back.

reviews.title: Great Experience
reviews.text: I would highly recommend this property.  It was just far enough removed from the strip to allow a quiet and enjoyable experience but close enough to be anywhere within a five to ten minute walk/ride.  Guest rooms are well appointed.  Pool and pool staff were delightful.  Staff was extremely friendly and attentive to all guests needs.  Another wonderful Four Seasons experience!

reviews.title: Elegance and Calm in Vegas
reviews.text: I recently spent three nights in Las Vegas for my first time and visited a different hotel each night. For anyone who is familiar with the Four Seasons brand they will know that the level of service and personalization is always a step above the competitors! The Four Seasons Las Vegas hotel is no exception. The hotel, located at the top of the Mandalay Bay complex is elegant, calm—quiet almost— although that is relatively speaking for Las Vegas, with a soothing decor that is typical of the Four Seasons brand— nothing garish or over the top, if you want that there are plenty of other hotels in the city. However, the rooms are divine: spacious, perfect bed (almost mythical) which is my favorite feature of the Four Seasons hotels (other than the personnel), with towels that were perfectly fluffy and the definition of what a true five-star hotel should have! The room was perfectly clean—no smell since the hotel is non-smoking and because they don’t pump nasty perfume all over the place like other hotels do. I loved using the Four Seasons mobile app that can provide you with service and suggestions which I took advantage of and found to be extremely responsive and awesome! Also, Ilove the L’Occitane bathroom amenities which are luxurious and high quality. (Although I have to admit that the almond scented line that they use is not my favorite—maybe they can switch to L’Occitane’s Bergamot and Jasmin line which is used at the Mexico City four seasons Hotel, which smells much better.) Pool service was prompt and very attentive. Breakfast at the Veranda restaurant was very good as well—efficient although not overly friendly (they might want to work on that) except for the lovely hostess, Fanny. And the cherry on top was that upon leaving when I asked for a taxi to the airport, Tony, at the front door surprised me by saying that he could take me in the hotel’s Mercedes-Benz car! Special shout out to Tony for being such a consummate professional and for the great conversation that we had on the brief trip to the airport. Although I plan on coming back regardless, Tony definitely sealed the deal with the kind of personalized service that the Four Seasons is so well known for.

reviews.title: A Serene Oasis
reviews.text: If the noise, crowds, long lines at check in, and walking through casinos to get to your room is not for you, this is the place to stay.  A quiet, peaceful oasis adjacent to the Mandalay Bay complex.   Actually it is in the same hotel building as Mandalay Bay but with a different entrance and lobby.  FS rooms are located on the higher floors.   The rooms are beautiful and comfortable.  The staff were extremely nice and helpful. The concierges were great.  There were complimentary drivers and cars to take us to the airport and restaurants elsewhere on the Strip.  We enjoyed excellent daily breakfasts at the Veranda Restaurant.  We ate at Charlie Parkers Steakhouse also located in the hotel one night.  Better than average but not great.  Like most Las Vegas restaurants overpriced and nothing special.  You will love your stay at the Four Seasons.

reviews.title: outstanding service all around
reviews.text: Excellent room, fully stocked mini-bar, housekeeping twice a day, high security easy touch key system; literally adjoining Mandalay Bay right outside the elevator. Very quiet room, very responsive heat/cooling system.  Great bathroom except for the toilet being in it's own "closet" with no outlet for a nightlight; who wants to turn on a bright light at night?  Had to prop that door open in order to avoid turning on overhead light.  All service people were so friendly and helpful, calling me by name most of the time! Expensive hotel but well worth it.  Pool and its staff were outstanding also, bringing towels and a full pitcher of ice water with the menu.  Room had a great plug-in area for all devices.

reviews.title: Fours Seasons Las Vegas
reviews.text: This is by far the best hotel on the strip. And I would strongly encourage you to visit the Spa.  I got the best manicure!  The staff is awesome and do whatever they can to please you .  It was one of the best trips to a hotel in a very long time.

reviews.title: Sublime
reviews.text: Stayed for a conference, and can't wait to return.  Room design, view, shower, tub, hair dryer, clothes steamer, bed, all A+. It was such a pleasure to go back to my room at the end of some very long days.  Housekeeping on my floor 36 was not so great. My colleague stayed on 35 floor.  For her, housekeeping paid extra attention to detail. Water by bedside replaced, counters  tidied up. But I'm still giving 5 stars, this place is sublime!

reviews.title: Elegance defined
reviews.text: Four Seasons have reminded me of what a 5 star experience should be...Every detail from arriving to departure was a spot on. The entire staff was genuine in nature, welcoming and ready to be of assistance if and when needed.

reviews.title: Absolute Perfection
reviews.text: The Four Seasons hotel is a gem, a quiet island of serenity in the sea of absolute madness that is Las Vegas.  Reading a description of the property one would think that it cannot avoid the lights, the glitter, the noise and thousands of tourists that otherwise overwhelm one’s senses and sensibilities but it manages to do so.  It’s 424 rooms are on the top four stories of the gargantuan 3209 room Mandalay Bay complex which includes a convention center, 5 swimming pools including a faux river and a huge wave machine, and hundreds of screaming children.  Mandalay Bay has its requisite multi-acre casino.  It is everything the Four Seasons is not.  On the other hand, even though it shares the site, the Four Seasons is a hotel within a hotel.  You can stay there and be totally oblivious to the huge complex around you.  The Four Seasons has its own private entrance, its own, quiet and calm, adults only swimming pool, separate elevators, separate everything including a superb restaurant, that serves 3 meals a day, including a great breakfast buffet.  The only real connection to Mandalay Bay complex is a very discreet door off the Lobby that opens right into the Casino complex of the Mandalay Bay itself.  Enter at your on peril.  It’s like entering another world.   There are no lines at check in or check out.  I saw a line of over 50 unhappy people waiting to check in at the Bellagio another gargantuan hotel on the strip.  It reminded me of the lines at busy Walmart cash registers on a Saturday afternoon.  At the Four Seasons you are greeted at the entrance and whisked through the check in process by staff.  Then you are accompanied to the private elevators, security personnel are always there, observing, checking, pushing the button to bring down the elevator cars while you are walking toward them.  The level of service provided by the hotel is extraordinary equal to any other Four Seasons in the world that I have stayed at.  I am really developing brand loyalty.  The guest rooms also meet Four Seasons standards of posh understated luxury.  Separate shower and tubs, double sinks, about 400-500 square feet of graciously appointed space.  Try to get a room with a city/strip view.  We were on the other side which had a view of the airport and the new football stadium.  But given that you are at least 35 floors up there are really no bad views.  The Mandalay Bay is slightly isolated, located near the end of the famous Las Vegas strip.  The other end is probably the Stratosphere, the iconic tower with its rides not for the faint of heart.  The distance between the 2 is about 6 miles. One major revelation about Las Vegas, where I never had been before, is the size of these hotel complexes, -the Forum, the Excalibur, the Bellagio and the like.  Some are near 5000 rooms, much larger than any hotel found in New York for example.  The would occupy between 5 and 10 NYC blocks.  Walking between hotels, especially on a 100+ degree day, in not really for the unfit.  Bring serious walking shoes.  After scouting out these iconic cities within cities, the tens of thousands of people scouting out the Strip you will be ever so glad to return to your sanctuary which is the Four Seasons.

reviews.title: Like coming home
reviews.text: We feel connected and loyal to this hotel because of the staff. We are recognised and warmly welcomed back. Rooms are luxurious with high end amenities.  Due to the high floors, there are no “bad” rooms. We love Vegas but not 24/7. This hotel has the exclusivity we desire - check in is never crowded, wonderful spa and the pool is a peaceful oasis. Wonderful staff at Press and Verandah.  Concierge team go out of their way to make our trip memorable, even long before we arrive. Dreaming of an opportunity to come back is never far from our minds.

reviews.title: Afternoon tea
reviews.text: My friend and I love the Afternoon Tea.  We were very Surprised to find out the tea is local from Wisconsin, very fresh.  The sandwich was delicious.  We also had a Halloween desserts.  The service was excellent.  Highly recommended for a relax afternoon with friends.

reviews.title: Elegant, relaxed hotel
reviews.text: I only stayed here one night, so I cannot provide a lot of information about the amenities (pool, spa, etc), and it may be 5 stars if I had been able to take advantage of them!  The lobby is elegant and relaxed and check in was a breeze. The rooms are nice and decent sized.  The casino is separate, which I really liked so that you don't feel like you are in a casino when you walk into the hotel.  The exercise room(s) are decent, but you have to walk through the spa and a maze of hallways to get there.  Overall, very nice just not quite the 5 star experience you get at some other Four Seasons, but definitely would stay here again.

reviews.title: Worth staying off the strip
reviews.text: If you are looking for a luxury hotel there's no other in Vegas like the Four Seasons. The location is perfect. It does not have a casino but the Mandalay is connected with very quick and easy access. It allows you to be in that "vegas space" when you want to be and remove yourself just the same.

reviews.title: Its the world's cheapest Four Season's for a reason
reviews.text: Located on the top few floors of the Mandalay Bay hotel, this is not a "real" Four Seasons. Don't expect the typical luxuries and solace that you would find at a typical Four Seasons hotel - if you see luxury pick the Wynn or Waldorf

reviews.title: Not the best four seasons but one of the better hotels in town
reviews.text: No gambling, boutique size and good service helps this dated four seasons win me over much thx to the credit of supervisor Jason Lou who offered great service when I had an issue with my room. It’s a hotel for the couples, families and others who prefers a bit more privacy than the bigger gambling hotels although they are very closely located.

reviews.title: Four Season - expensive but nice
reviews.text: nice hotel with great bed. The front desk is a little impersonal. Attached to Mandalay bay hotel and casino. howerver there is no annoying slot machines in the lobby. Be ready for restaurant and bar costs - outragious, bacon and eggs =$24. breakfast is $40+

reviews.title: Great hotel ... unfortunate location
reviews.text: This was our first stay at the Four Seasons.  The couple we traveled with wanted a non-casino hotel.  They had previously stayed here, and we had been a few times to  the (now) Waldorf Astoria.We were happy to give this property a try based on their recommendation.Overall, the hotel is fine.  The service is impeccable, the staff goes out of its way to check and and see if there is anything they can do for you at every turn.  The private entrance to both the hotel and the adjacent facilities adds just the perfect amount of exclusivity.The pool can get a bit crowded, so get there early to have chairs set up for you.  But again, the pool staff is quite spectacular, and the area is a nice place to spend the day.There are however, a few things that will probably keep us from returning.1.  Our room was in the wing that faced the end of the airport runway.  While I can not speak to the other parts of the hotel, when the planes started taking off at about 6 A.M. it was far too noisy to sleep.  2.  This is certainly not the fault of the property, but the casino at Mandalay Bay is quite tired.  It felt to us as though it was in desperate need of a refresh and update.  The byproduct of this is that you do not have the energy and ambiance that a higher end facility would have.  We commented how nice it would be if the Four Seasons sat on top of the Aria, or Wynn.Overall, I would recommend this property if those two issues we insignificant to you.

reviews.title: Just perfect
reviews.text: We are highly satisfied! ...thank you for your kindness and your excellent service! Thank you for taking such Good care of us (we love your staff!) ...we are sure that we will visit you again soon :) !

reviews.title: Not worth the price
reviews.text: At $280 per night your would expect luxurious accommodations, attentive and friendly service and a large comfortable room.  None of these hold true for the Four Seasons.  The Hotel is not close to any other part of the strip, but is right next to the airport so planes and helicopters fligh close by every 30 minutes.

reviews.title: Oasis within Chaos
reviews.text: Great hotel, the Mandalay Bay Casino leaves much to be desired. No one is there, it's like the shooter is still firing away. I was literally the last blackjack player in the casio on a Wed night. But that's Mandalay's problem. Too bad the Four Seasons wasn't located mid-strip.

reviews.title: Our second stay... and likely our last.
reviews.text: Unfortunately, there are only few hotels in Las Vegas that you can stay and get away from the ridiculous experience of being forced to walk through a noisy casino each time you come or go.  Either you go for a suite that offers private entrance access (such as the Wynn towers) or you pick a non casino hotel such as the Four Seasons or Waldorf Astoria (formerly Mandarin Oriental). I really wanted to like this Four Seasons, as we have stayed in many around the world and experienced not only luxury but exceptional service.  Alas... this is Vegas, and having a separate entrance and rebranding the top floors of the Mandalay Bay just doesn't meet that standard.  The rooms are noisy, with poor glass sound insulation, and the hallway noise is very apparent... especially at 3am when the drunks stumble home!  The rooms are descent sized, and the bed is Four Seasons comfortable, but as others have mentioned, doesn't look like a standard King size.  Service was also average... valets should really learn some manners and know to always open the door for a lady!! The veranda restaurant offers a good buffet for breakfast, all be it at Four Seasons prices.  Overall, a 4 star property.  I was skeptical after our first stay... the second will be our last.

reviews.title: Top Quality Service, rooms not that good.
reviews.text: Services is as always in all Four seasons, the best experencie. The infrastructure of the Hotel is limited and the rooms are very average compared to any other Four Seasons. Food quality is great, amazing restaurants,  pool is average but the Staff makes looks everything amazing!

reviews.title: Amazing As Always!
reviews.text: The customer servuce is excellent. The pool staff is very accomodating and the pool is amazing. The beds are so comfortable and the linens they use are superb. I look forward to coming back soon. Thank you Four Seasons!

reviews.title: Would be amazing anywhere else but not in vegas
reviews.text: Its interesting as this hotel is nestled within the mandalay bay resort and hwile it has its very own entrance, facilities and pool you feel like you are piggybacking on it. So don't get me wrong anywhere else this hotel would be outstanding, but having stayed in many other vegas hotel, the only thing that makes this special is the extraordinary service the staff provide.

reviews.title: Great Las Vegas Experience. Highly Recommended
reviews.text: There is not too much to be said. We had a great, as ever, Four Seasons experience in the Las Vegas hotel from friendly valet and check in, an amazing suite with full Las Vegas Strip view, great service through, both breakfast and dinner and at the pool. It is a great "family place" as well as much more quite than the other hotels and a nice breakout from the rest of Las Vegas. I can certainly recommend this hotel fully to everybody.

reviews.title: Great Sanctuary in the Chaos of Vegas
reviews.text: Stayed here with my kids and it was amazing. I highly recommend it. Great service and amenities and the pool was great and much appreciated. Close enough to the Mandalay Bay pool that it was easy to go back and forth, but fantastic on its own, too. Great service at this hotel that exemplifies the Four Seasons standard. If I'm back to Vegas, I'll definitely stay here again.

reviews.title: Best Service in Las Vegas
reviews.text: The service at this hotel was top notch! We spent most of our time by the beautiful relaxing pool. All of the staff at the pool were fabulous during our stay. They always made sure our drinks were refilled and they continued to bring us fresh ice water throughout the day. We especially loved the frozen fruit and treats that were passed out all day long.All of the employees we came into contact with were so friendly and helpful especially the pool attendants, parking attendants, elevator attendants, housekeeping, and the front desk. I really wish we would've gotten the names of the employees but honestly everyone we came into contact with were wonderful. The rooms were sparkling clean and and the bedding was so comfortable and luxurious. We slept well.Thank you for a fantastic stay! We hope to be back again soon.

reviews.title: One of the best in Vegas
reviews.text: I took my family to Las Vegas in August 2019. We stayed at the Four Seasons since it was also an anniversary trip for my wife and I wanted to stay somewhere special that was kid friendly.      The service here is top notch! 👌 we spent most of our time relaxing by the pool. It’s quiet and has excellent poolside service from the staff! Every hour or so they come by with treats for all the guests at the pool. As a Four Seasons guest, you also have access to the Mandalay Bay pools. They have the lazy river and wave pool, which we loved. However, when you’re tired of the huge crowds and craziness at Mandalay Bay, it’s an easy, short walk back to the relaxing Four Seasons pool. (Mandalay guests don’t have access to the FS pool but you have access to theirs!     We had a room on a high floor and were upgraded to a strip view! The gym is good and comes with a steam room and lockers. Gusts have 24/7 access but after 9 you need to contact the front desk to be let in since the gym staff leave at 9. I highly recommend the Four Seasons in Las Vegas!

reviews.title: Excellent stay for a family in Vegas!
reviews.text: Our family had a wonderful nights stay at the Four Seasons Las Vegas, after touring Utah National Parks.  Great option for children in Vegas! Really appreciated the no smoking, no gaming environment.  Our suite was immaculate, great service.  Our children were treated to chocolate chip cookies and color changing sunglasses upon arrival.  It was easygoing to the Blue Man Group from the Four Seasons.  Nice having the Mandalay aquarium and Mandalay restaurant row a short walk away (though have to cross casino to access these.) Would definitely recommend the Four Seasons Las Vegas for a family stay in Vegas!

reviews.title: A peaceful stay in Vegas
reviews.text: A wonderfully peaceful weekend in Vegas — this hotel shields you from the craziness on the Strip in many ways, but is close to everything. No casino = quiet lobby and no smoke. The pool (for hotel guests only) is an oasis of calm, no music playing (children are allowed but it wasn’t lots of kids screaming). Nice gym too. Attentive service in the hotel & pool also. Definitely recommended.

reviews.title: Luxury in every sense of the word
reviews.text: A. No gambling in the lobbyB. Quiet, spacious and comfortable entrance.C. Great service from the entire staff.D. Room was large, well lit with an excellent bathrooom (super shower).E. Food was probably the weak link, but not enough to cost a star.F. They replaced my tattered mouse pad with a bran new one, which I still use. Thank you.

reviews.title: Oasis on the Strip
reviews.text: This was my first time staying at this hotel.  I went with my sister for a weekend getaway.  We loved the furnishings and the valet was quick and attentive.  Also, they did a great job furnishing us with free water in our room and at the valet daily.  My sister ordered room service for breakfast one morning and it was served within 15 minutes of ordering.  I would stay here again!

reviews.title: Amazing Experience
reviews.text: I stayed here from September 28-30 with my wife, my 6 year old daughter, and my 2 year old daughter.  We drove in from Los Angeles and were able to check in when we arrived at 1 pm and were given room 35121 with a fantastic view of the Las Vegas strip.  We had notified the Director of Rooms, Austin Price, that our daughters were with us and the girls were ecstatic when they walked in the room and saw 2 stuffed animals, 2 customized bags, and 2 candy trays (m&m's, gummy bears, rice krispy pops, cookie pops, etc.) waiting for them.  There was also a fruit tray and some premium water for the grown ups as well.  We had a bunch of friends and family staying at Mandalay Bay so we met them down at the pool.  The Four Seasons has its own private pool area but we spent all of our time at Mandalay Beach which we absolutely love, but staying at the FS is great because you have the option of using both pools and while the main pool area can get really crowded (it was hard to find seats for a large group btw), there always appeared to be plenty of chairs available at the FS pool.  My girls had a great time at the lazy river and loved circling around and passing through the waterfall over and over again.On our second day we took the girls to the Shark Reef Aquarium which I highly recommend for families.  It's a first class aquarium with a very interesting collection of sharks, fish, crocodiles, octopuses, stingrays, etc.  Everyone really enjoyed the visit there.The housekeeping staff at the FS was fantastic with daily cleanings and nightly turn down service.  The room and bathroom were in perfectly maintained during our stay.  The complex is at the south end of the strip so it's a bit of a trek but with a monorail and plenty of taxi/ubers available it's easy to get around and then return to an area that's not as congested as other parts of the strip.  We loved our trip and will definitely return.

reviews.title: Make this your get away for a reason or a season!
reviews.text: This was our first visit to a 4 Seasons property as the trip was an anniversary gift from our daughter and her husband. From the moment we chose Las Vegas 4 Seasons we were immersed in a world of beauty, relaxation, attentiveness and deliciousness.  You must experience this oasis in the desert!

reviews.title: Great stay at a great hotel
reviews.text: From the moment we arrived until the moment we departed, we were treated warmly and very professionally. This was a quick weekend getaway trip and the Four Seasons hotel made our trip very successful. Many thanks.

reviews.title: Everything we expect from Four Seasons
reviews.text: This hotel is terrific.  It's actually five floors (35-39) of the Mandalay Bay.  There are separate operations down to a key card entrance to the hotel elevator on the casino level.  Here's a tip: room rates are very responsive to demand.  We stayed Sept. 29-Oct. 2.  The rates skyrocketed on Oct. 3 because Aerosmith fans booked the hotel solid.  If your travel plans are flexible, try various dates.  When you get to the front desk, ask about upgrading to a suite.  Beware of the add-on fees.  Valet parking is $32/day with unllimited in-out privileges.  There is a resort fee of $39/day.  We did not have time to take advantage of access to six swimming poois.

reviews.title: Long walk
reviews.text: Only valet at this location. The thought of strangers in our car, and having the key to the car is always unsettling, especially when the car is loading with stuff. The self parking available is at Mandalay Bay. Long, long walk. The hotel is a hotel within a hotel, essentially 5 floors of Mandalay Bay is Four Seasons. Different entrance making check in a long walk. After checking in, the walk to the elevator is quit long as well. We enjoy walking, but not with suitcases.

reviews.title: Watch out! Not a King bed!
reviews.text: My wife and I stayed at the Four Seasons Las Vegas this past weekend. Large and nicely decorated room, but the king bed felt oddly small.  The room we booked was a king bedroom, however the bed did not measure up to a king size bed; my wife was convinced that it felt like a queen. We raised our concerns with management, and their response was that they only have king beds or 2 doubles in the rooms. With that they offered to come up and measure. We asked what size king they had, and the front desk manager Carlos (Manager #1) said it was a standard North American King which is 76" x 80" (6.3 by 6.66 feet).  This was not the case as he pulled out a measuring tape and measured 69" x 77".  Carlos couldn't tell us why the bed did not measure up to be a proper king size bed.  He said he would send up the Housekeeping Manager - Kyle (Manager #2); he came up to measure, but Kyle provided a different answer. Specifically that it should be a California King, which is narrower but longer at 72" x 84".  However his measurement fell short as well at 70" x 77". He stated that this is the king size bed in all of their king rooms, but could not provide an explanation as to why they didn’t measure up to a California King.The last manager we spoke to when checking out, Chadd (Manager #3) provided us with a third answer; that it was a "Four Season's King", which basically means they are making up their own bed size standards. Essentially a Four Seasons foot is not 12" but rather 11" >>> or any arbitrary sizes they choose it to be. We are big fans of the Four Seasons, making this experience extremely disappointing. That a hotel of Four Seasons’ stature is misrepresenting what you as a consumer is purchasing, thus short changing you just feels wrong. For anyone staying at Four Seasons Las Vegas right now, or planning to go, please measure the bed for yourself, or have a manager measure for you - you’ll feel short changed!

reviews.title: A great stay
reviews.text: We stayed here for 3 nights and were impressed but not surprised as Four Seasons have never disappointed us yet. Good location for us as we liked being at the end of the strip and yet we could walk to most places or you can go part way down the strip on the free tram. Lovely room with strip view and very quiet. Breakfast in restaurant was good on the first day and then the other days we found it handy to go to the coffee and muffin place which operates in the morning, in the lobby - great idea.We enjoyed a couple of afternoons by the pool where there were plenty of sun beds, staff were very cheerful and attentive and the food service was excellent. We also used the treadmills in the fitness centre which were good. Although it seems to be part of/ linked to the Mandalay Bay it still had the smaller feel we like and we were glad we stayed here after seeing the check in queues at some of the much larger hotels. Would definitely recommend this hotel.

reviews.title: Always Exceptional
reviews.text: Always have an exceptional stay at the Las Vegas Four Seasons.    From top to bottom, everything is superb.   Staff / Accommodations / Dining, just awesome.    From Check-In to Departure, could not ask for a simpler and more pleasant experience throughout!

reviews.title: Still the best in Las Vegas
reviews.text: Returning to FS after several years of staying in other properties in Las Vegas, we cane back to a refreshing and refreshed hotel. It remains a calming, relaxing respite in a city of chaos, and every staff member, to the person, made us feel welcome and coddled. We will return here again and again.

reviews.title: If I could give 10 stars I would!
reviews.text: Low key hotel with Exceptional service. The food in the hotel is amazing...especially the breakfast buffet they offer. Hands down the best brunch I’ve been to.The pool area is very clean and quiet.You don’t lack for anything here. First class in every way.

reviews.title: What a peaceful hotel stay in the town that never sleeps
reviews.text: Awesome...one of the best Hotels I have stayed in all my travels around the word...in over 45 years of travel...never have I ever been so pleased from a personal and business prospective!!  Highly recommend the oasis in the desert called Las Vegas.

reviews.title: Another great stay
reviews.text: After a long week of meetings and a conference, I was gathering my luggage from the bellman and asked about my stay and where I was headed. I mentioned I was tired and ready to get home. His next sentence was unexpected, most welcomed and music to my ears. "George, would you please take Mr. Moore to the airport" A perfect ending to a wonderful stay.

reviews.title: Just perfect
reviews.text: From the personal greeting on our arrival to the accommodation made on our departure day, the staff went out of their way to make us feel special. We couldn’t recommend this hotel more highly. A delightful quiet island in a sea of chaos.

reviews.title: A quality flaw the FS brand should not tolerate
reviews.text: We (my wife and me) have never been great fans of Las Vegas, but oddly ended up there a number of times. Once for a concert, once while driving East to West etc... this time was for the Aerosmith's gig (a delusion on its own). We decided to go for one hotel that could keep us away from the gambling crowds and let us sleep somehow without having to join the next door guests in their noisy fun. A secluded resort, with the service level and all the comforts which normally comes with the Four Seasons brand. So we opted for the Four Seasons Las Vegas, which from the website looks like a completely different thing, mostly because it says it's a 'non-gaming sanctuary' and boasts award-winning dining. We took a one bedroom suite with mountains view. At our arrival we finally understood what being within the Mandalay Bay meant (something we did not consider properly): far from the heart of Vegas and still attached to a massive gambling and conferencing hub - quite a busy one.One thing is worth mentioning, the price it tag is (at least that's what we paid) twice the one of any other main hotel in Vegas!The staff is very polite, welcoming and helpful. Only reason why I would give a 3/5 and not a deserved 2!The hotel on its own... is surely not as elegant as you would expect from a Four Seasons. It is quite standard, clean, but just massive and 'average'. Given the massive dimensions it looks even more 'corporate' and anonymous. Room very nice, large, but noisy - the room is basically overlooking the nearby airport... like you are on the runaway! The bed is far too soft and could have been larger given the large size of the room.Cleaning and refilling of the room... some flaws. Can't stand when they forget to refill the minibar.Dining - very very disappointing. The quality is surely not award-winning, not recently at least. Good may be. For the price charged for in room dining, you would expect excellence. The major disappointment was the speed of service. From order to room in average 45 minutes it's a bit too much. Restaurants downstairs operate only in certain hours and the cafeteria for a quick breakfast is worse than a standard Starbucks.Sorry, but it has been a less than average experience, surely not FS brand should be accepting. Massive

reviews.title: Great stay in a beautiful room
reviews.text: We have been to Vegas dozens of times over several decades and have stayed at many excellent hotels. Our conference was at the Mandalay Bay, and our reservation date was incorrect (our fault). We were not excited about staying there anyway and called the Four Seasons, who had availability. From check-in to check-out, Jacob was gracious, friendly, and showed true hospitality. We appreciated his effort in securing us a lovely room with a view. The housekeeping team also did a fantastic job of keeping our room tidy and well-supplied throughout our several days there; they were always polite when we saw them. (Please have someone clean the ceiling vents in both bathrooms as they were heavily dusty!). We had a brief time to enjoy the pool, which is a nice oasis in the middle of the Mandalay commotion; you truly feel removed from the other property. Only a minor complaint there - we were taken to poolside chairs immediately, but the server did not come over for 15 minutes and then informed us last call would be in 10 minutes. They probably need to acknowledge the newly seated guests a lot faster. The pool was not packed with people at all. We have stayed at multiple Four Seasons properties and enjoyed this one; we will be back on a future trip to Vegas!

reviews.title: A little less fabulous than usual
reviews.text: We stayed at the FS Las Vegas 17-20 September. We love the hotel, have stayed here consistently for 19 years. Love the fact it’s non-gaming.  Love the breakfast by the pool. Love the pool! Love the privacy! We had all of those things this time. And it’s worth giving kudos to the ladies in the spa who were very friendly and accommodating. Catherine gave an awesome pedicure and was an absolute delight to chat with during the treatment. Our room was spotless and beautifully prepared every day. Housekeeping were splendid. But a few things took the shine off our stay. We had some issues at check-in, and despite being on a special TA package, no upgrades were available (though part of the package (if available)........we had pre-paid our rate 3 months previously which meant we had overpaid for our room at the rates of the day of arrival, and though it took a little bargaining (which I didn’t enjoy!), we did have the difference credited to our room..........I asked for a later check-out the day before leaving, but they could only manage 30 minutes free, and wanted to charge for 2 hours (really, for guests that have been staying at the hotel for 19 years?!?). We’re really low maintenance guests, and would have appreciated a little bit of give on that issue.........There wasn’t much of a warm greeting at the pool on the two mornings we sat by the pool from the same staff member...........and no Evian spritz!...........The night before leaving, went to make an in room coffee - found only one decaf capsule - we needed two - and when the long life milk was poured, it was lumpy and clearly was past it’s use by date. It was late and I didn’t want to wait have more brought to the room late at night..............At check-out, there was a line (which I have never seen before at the FS), and only two people at the desk, which meant that my check-out was somewhat hasty and meant the agent didn’t check on my stay......... I know these are details, but I expect (I think reasonably?) pretty much perfection at the Four Seasons. It’s usually like staying in heaven. It was still heavenly, but the clouds weren’t quite as soft on this trip! We’ll be back, but please, keep an eye on those important little details. (And noticed the plaque for Mark at the front of the hotel - a lovely thing to do, and very touching).

reviews.title: Great Stay
reviews.text: Stayed at Four Seasons Las Vegas beginning 9/18/2019 through 9/20/2019.  Great stay as always.  Impeccable staff and wonderful property.  Highly recommend!  Veranda is a great spot for lunch.  The pool is wonderful.  The second floor casino entrance to Mandalay is also really excellent because you can still get easy access to the casino but can escape back to the comfort of FS very easily when you've had enough of the smoke and lights and craziness of the casino.

reviews.title: An Oasis of Pure Bliss
reviews.text: My husband and I just got back from a week long trip for my birthday. We had two nights on the ocean and four nights at the Four Seasons Las Vegas. While the whole trip was wonderful, our time at the Four Seasons was definitely the highlight. From the moment we arrived we felt so welcomed and throughout our stay that feeling remained. Check in was an absolute breeze and we were given an upgraded room because we were there for my birthday. Our room had an absolutely fabulous view of the strip. I don't think it couldn't have been a lovelier view or room. The bed was extremely comfortable and we slept extremely well each night. We spend quite a bit of time at the pool which is beautiful and never crowded (at least when we were there). So relaxing and the perfect spot to order breakfast or lunch or a pina colada and just feel pampered. The frozen snickers, peppermint patties and pineapple were a fun touch that we appreciated. All of the poolside employees were friendly, helpful, and great overall. We ate twice at The Veranda, once for breakfast and once for lunch. Both meals were delicous and the ambience as we sat outside near the pool area was just perfect! The day we checked out was hard because we truly did not want to leave. We are definitely spoiled going forward and will always stay at the Four Seasons when in Vegas. We have stayed at many hotels on the strip and this one is beyond compare to any of them. If you decide to stay here, you will love love love every minute of your stay and will be so very glad that you chose the Four Seasons. We have stayed at only one other Four Seasons property (in Maui) which was also absolutely amazing. Our new goal is to stay at as many of their properties as we can in the years ahead. I hope that will be quite a few! :)

reviews.title: Amazing non-gaming oasis in Vegas
reviews.text: I know - "non-gaming" and "Vegas" sound like contradictions - but the Four Seasons is a perfect solution for people who want both.  Nestled next to the gaming-intense Mandalay Bay Resort, the Four Seasons is a gorgeous oasis of quiet, calm luxury.  From the beautiful rooms, to the attentive staff, to the delicious food, to the wonderful spa and pool ... the Four Seasons really is an oasis within the Strip.  We will be back!

reviews.title: Best hotel without casino !
reviews.text: If you want a peaceful luxurious environment this is the right place to go in las vegas ! At the end of the strip but sharing same facility with Mandalay hotel.Rooms are very cosy and not so pricey. The gym is pretty good and they offer Gatorade.The restaurants are not outstanding but fine for some meals Some rooms are far from the elevator so you need to walk some but nothing compared to The other resorts like the Caesars palace or similars.Easy and very fast check in ...Very friendly staff everywhere Nice pool with tanning creams offered spf 15 or 30 !Small details that make a difference!

reviews.title: Luxury with just enough distance from the hustle of the strip
reviews.text: From the time we got out of the car to check-out the hospitality staff at the Four Seasons was top notch.  We even had the wait staff at very, early morning hours asked us if we needed water at the gym.  The pool, though small in size, had very attentive wait staff handing out frozen pineapples and peppermint patties and water.  It was a perfect two night stay during a weekend when you want to GO to Vegas but not be in the crush of the tourist mecca.  It's a bit removed from the other main sights like the Bellagio, etc, but walkable.  What I liked most is that it felt more like a luxury boutique hotel where we got to drop in on Vegas when we needed.  Versus some of the other major hotels where you can't escape the Vegas extreme vibe.  The no smoking helps a lot.  You walk in - and feel like you're transported away from the Strip.

reviews.title: Perfect Service & Experience
reviews.text: Love the app.  Appreciated the excellent valet service and quick front desk checkin.  The guest elevators are a bit of a hike, but you pass the spa and a shop or two, so the walk informs you of some options.The hotel shares space with Mandalay Bay, even allowing access to the Mandalay Beach Pool, restaurants, and casino.  We had previously stayed at the Bellagio in a suite, but everything there was dated, and had an odor (people, lots of smoke).  NO odors at the Four Seasons and the decor is refined elegance.  Robes, L’Occitan toiletries, and upscale minibar assortment, a small safe, and a Keurig (something Bellagio lacked) rounded out the amenities.I used the pool, and the staff were nicely attentive.  One hiccup...  I had a Woodford Reserve old fashioned... just regular maraschino cherries?!?  In today’s upscale cocktail world, that’s a “no-no”.  (I have faith it will be corrected in the near future.)The room service breakfast was PERFECT; my husbands eggs and bacon were still hot, the coffee was good, and the fresh OJ was perfect.  The yogurt was homemade, and delicious.  And the muffins and fruit quality and assortment were EXCELLENT.Thank you for a great last night in Vegas.

reviews.title: Best Hotel in Las Vegas
reviews.text: Great service with attention to detail. No noisy people and pool water warm with great service. Check in is fast and staff makes you feel at home. Food at the Veranda is excellent with great service and quality.

reviews.title: Perfect Hotel
reviews.text: Love the no smoking and no gambling, but yet connected to everything you may want. The best of both worlds with Four Season treatment.Check-in is easy, amenities perfect without the large crowds. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Still knocks my socks off!
reviews.text: I love this hotel!   It just gets better and better.  It’s been awhile since I’d stayed there.  They have added a lobby bar which is a great gathering spot (but I wish they had a separate bar for conference attendees.  The bar menu is very good (I preferred it to Charlie Palmer).  Ross the bartender was terrific.  But, the bar closed a bit early for us.  The rooms have been remodeled.  This place is a true respite from the chaos of Las Vegas. Easy check in.  I can’t say enough great stuff.

reviews.title: Girls getaway
reviews.text: Excellent stay. Staff was friendly and rooms were well appointed. A bit tucked away from the action if you like to be a bit out of the fray and quite. Pool was very pleasant and staff was attentive to our needs

reviews.title: Amazing luxury!
reviews.text: The Four Seasons Las Vegas really understands what luxury means, and they deliver!  Service is impeccable, and no request is too difficult. I wish I could only stay at Four Seasons hotels!  I stay there every chance I get.

reviews.title: Stately, elegant hotel.
reviews.text: Located bear Mandalay Bay, this is a regal hotel. Lobby area, with bars is stunning. Beautiful decor and tastefully designed. Service staff very coordinated and eager to please. Veranda Restaurant is well worth the ride up the Strip.

reviews.title: Best hotel .
reviews.text: This hotel remains my absolute favorite... quality in food, service ( all levels), and overall beauty. I choose the same suite , and it’s flattering that staff remember me from last year. 5⭐️I promise- you’ll love it.

reviews.title: The Best Of The Best 2019
reviews.text: This place is on another level for so many reasons. The main thing is the staff and the level of service that the provide. It will literally change your whole view on a Vegas experience. Also the pool here is so relaxing.

reviews.title: One of the best in Las Vegas!!
